title: SNT-TC-1A Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Any US inspection service provider whose customer, code or purchase order invokes SNT-TC-1A: weld and fabrication NDT under ASME BPVC Section V and Section.
h1: SNT-TC-1A Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Any US inspection service provider whose customer, code or purchase order invokes SNT-TC-1A: weld and fabrication NDT under ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII, structural work under AWS D1. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: 1, refinery, piping and tank work under the API inspection codes, and pipeline construction where 49 CFR 192.243 requires NDT performed to written procedures by trained, qualified persons. facets.q: Who does SNT-TC-1A apply to?
facets.a: Any US inspection service provider whose customer, code or purchase order invokes SNT-TC-1A: weld and fabrication NDT under ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII, structural work under AWS D1.1, refinery, piping and tank work under the API inspection codes, and pipeline construction where 49 CFR 192.243 requires NDT performed to written procedures by trained, qualified persons. It binds the firm's qualification programme, not the individual technician.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for SNT-TC-1A compliance?
facets.a: Yes. SNT-TC-1A accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a SNT-TC-1A audit ask for?
facets.a: Written Practice for the control and administration of NDT personnel training, examination and certification, approved by the employer's NDT Level III and retained on file, NDT Level III qualification records — ASNT NDT Level III certificates, or the outside-agency Level III agreement plus that person's credentials, Training records showing classroom hours per method and level against the SNT-TC-1A training table, with content traceable to ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outlines, Documented on-the-job experience with dates, method, and supervisor attestation, General, specific and practical examination records, graded answer sheets, and the Level III-approved examination question bank. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is SNT-TC-1A renewed?
facets.a: Recertification is periodic and the interval is fixed by the employer's own Written Practice, not by ASNT. ASNT describes a recommended maximum interval of five years between renewals for NDT personnel. Recertification requires evidence of continued competence — re-examination or documented continuing activity — plus current vision records. Accreditation of the programme itself under the ASNT EBC route runs three years, with some registrations on one-year terms requiring annual surveillance. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common SNT-TC-1A findings?
facets.a: Written Practice is a copy of the standard rather than a description of how the firm actually trains, examines and certifies, Examination question bank not approved by the NDT Level III, or reused without control, Certification examination administered by the candidate, or by someone the candidate supervises, On-the-job experience recorded without traceable dates, methods or supervisor attestation. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does SNT-TC-1A cover?
facets.a: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, CR/DR, MT, PT, VT. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

facets.q: How long does SNT-TC-1A audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does American Society for Nondestructive Testing (ASNT) publishes it. Nobody enforces SNT-TC-1A directly — it becomes binding when a code, customer or regulator invokes it (ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII, AWS D1.1, the API inspection codes, prime purchase orders). ASNT Certification Services LLC will audit and accredit a firm's programme against it through the Employer-Based Certification (EBC) Accreditation Program. look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common SNT-TC-1A findings?
facets.a: Written Practice is a copy of the standard rather than a description of how the firm actually trains, examines and certifies, Examination question bank not approved by the NDT Level III, or reused without control, Certification examination administered by the candidate, or by someone the candidate supervises, On-the-job experience recorded without traceable dates, methods or supervisor attestation. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the SNT-TC-1A audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a SNT-TC-1A finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does SNT-TC-1A require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first SNT-TC-1A audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What documents does a CP-189 audit ask for?

facets.q: How often is CP-189 renewed?
facets.a: CP-189 makes recertification a requirement rather than a recommendation, with the interval fixed in the firm's certification procedure. The dependent credential has a firm published number: the ASNT NDT Level III certificate the CP-189 Level III must hold is renewed every five years, either by accumulating a minimum of 25 recertification points across the 60-month cycle while maintaining at least 36 months (756 days) per method of active Level III work, or by retaking and passing the examinations before the expiry date. facets.q: What are the most common CP-189 findings?

facets.q: How long does CP-189 audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the CP-189 audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a CP-189 finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does CP-189 require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first CP-189 audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: Does CP-189 require a separate procedure for UT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a UT procedure under CP-189?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in UT. Because CP-189 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover UT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What UT records does a CP-189 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's UT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, cables, couplant, and the calibration and reference blocks used to set sensitivity. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common UT finding at audit?
facets.a: An in-calibration instrument used with an unidentified or out-of-calibration reference block. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under CP-189 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform UT under CP-189?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does UT need under CP-189?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do UT requirements differ from the other methods in CP-189?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. CP-189 also covers PAUT, TOFD, RT, CR/DR/CT image interpretation, MT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

facets.q: Does CP-189 require a separate procedure for RT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a RT procedure under CP-189?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in RT. Because CP-189 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover RT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What RT records does a CP-189 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's RT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — source or tube, exposure devices, film or detectors, densitometers, IQIs and the survey meters used to control the area. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common RT finding at audit?
facets.a: IQI sensitivity not achieved, or radiation area control records missing for the shot. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under CP-189 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform RT under CP-189?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

title: ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Individual technicians and Level IIIs at US inspection service providers whose clients require third-party, ISO 9712-style certification rather than an employer cert
h1: ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Individual technicians and Level IIIs at US inspection service providers whose clients require third-party, ISO 9712-style certification rather than an employer certificate — international EPC contracts, export fabrication, offshore and marine scopes, and buyers who will not accept employer-signed credentials. Personnel certification is central or third-party here, so the firm cannot certify its own technicians internally.
expansion: It also applies to any firm still carrying legacy ACCP certificates, which are inside a closing transition window. The programme named in most older specifications no longer exists under that name. ASNT retired the ASNT Central Certification Program (ACCP) and replaced it with the ASNT 9712 Certification Program, launched by ASNT Certification Services LLC in March 2023 and built on ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (ISO 9712:2021):2023, the ANSI-approved identical adoption of ISO 9712:2021. For an inspection service provider this is a personnel credential, not a company accreditation: it certifies the individual, travels with the technician, and cannot be signed for by a contracted Level III. ASNT's implementation choices inside the ISO framework include an 80% pass mark on practical examinations, mandatory flaw detection, psychometric validation of practical assessments, and acceptance of employer-based training certificates as qualifying documentation.
source: ASNT newsroom, 'Important Update to ACCP and CWI/SCWI Certification Program' (asnt.org) — verbatim dates: new applications stopped 15 May 2023, renewals stopped 30 August 2023, transition to September 2028, 24-month CWI/SCWI extension from 1 July 2023. ASNT Materials Evaluation, 'Understanding ASNT 9712: How It Relates to ISO 9712 and What Sets It Apart' (asnt.org/me/26/8) — identical adoption, 80% practical pass mark, mandatory flaw detection, psychometric validation, acceptance of employer-based training certificates, ACCP retirement with last certifications expiring 2029, and the statement that ASNT is pursuing ANAB ISO/IEC 17024 accreditation for ASNT 9712. ASNT 9712 Level II and Level III certification pages, certification.asnt.org — training days, experience days, exam structure, five-year validity, ten-year training validity, and published fees (Level II single technique US$1,270 member / US$1,345 non-member; multi-technique bundles US$1,620–1,970 member; Level III packages roughly US$1,190–1,820 member depending on method and whether the candidate already holds ASNT NDT Level III; individual exam components US$120–655). ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (2023) listed on asnt.org/standards-publications/standards as the US adoption of ISO 9712:2021. All checked August 2026.

facets.q: Who does ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) apply to?
facets.a: Individual technicians and Level IIIs at US inspection service providers whose clients require third-party, ISO 9712-style certification rather than an employer certificate — international EPC contracts, export fabrication, offshore and marine scopes, and buyers who will not accept employer-signed credentials. It also applies to any firm still carrying legacy ACCP certificates, which are inside a closing transition window.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) compliance?
facets.a: Not for the certification itself. ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) requires central or third-party personnel certification, so technicians are certified by the scheme rather than by the employer. A consulting Level III still adds value on procedures, documentation, gap assessment and audit attendance — but cannot substitute for the scheme's own certification.

facets.q: What documents does a ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) audit ask for?
facets.a: ASNT 9712 application naming method, level and the practical technique coverage sought (single technique, or all techniques for the method), Employer-signed verification of industrial NDT experience, expressed in days per method, Training certificates evidencing the required days of training, dated inside the ten-year validity window, Level II certificate or equivalent evidence where applying for Level III by the Level II route, Vision examination evidence — near vision acuity and colour vision. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) renewed?
facets.a: Certificates run five years and are renewed through a structured credit-point system rather than automatic re-examination; technical training supporting the initial certification stays valid for a maximum of ten years. ACCP transition dates are fixed and published: ASNT stopped accepting first-time ACCP applications on 15 May 2023 and stopped renewing existing ACCP certificants on 30 August 2023, with a transition period running to September 2028 when the ACCP programme sunsets. A 2026 ASNT article describes the last active ACCP certifications expiring in 2029. A restricted ACCP Level II VT route for AWS CWI/SCWI holders was extended by 24 months beginning 1 July 2023 by agreement between ASNT and AWS. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) findings?
facets.a: Firm assumes its employer-issued SNT-TC-1A certificates satisfy a client's ISO 9712 requirement — they do not, because ASNT 9712 certifies the person against a third-party scheme, Training certificates older than the ten-year validity window submitted as qualifying documentation, Experience verification supplied as hours or a job title rather than supervised days per method, Practical examination failed on flaw detection, which is mandatory under ASNT's implementation of the scheme. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) cover?
facets.a: MT (bench, yoke), PT (three techniques), RT (gamma, X-ray), UT (straight beam, angle beam), VT (direct, remote — announced by ASNT as coming, not yet released). Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. facets.q: What happens after a ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) finding?

facets.q: Does ASNT 9712 (formerly ACCP) require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. title: NAS 410 / EN 4179 Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: NDT providers and in-house NDT functions serving aerospace manufacturing, maintenance, repair and overhaul — engine and airframe shops, casting and forging suppliers
h1: NAS 410 / EN 4179 Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: NDT providers and in-house NDT functions serving aerospace manufacturing, maintenance, repair and overhaul — engine and airframe shops, casting and forging suppliers, and independent NDT houses on aerospace approved-supplier lists. Primes flow the requirement down through purchase orders, and Nadcap audits it under AC7114. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: Firms selling into both US and European aerospace supply chains have to satisfy the NAS 410 and EN 4179 halves consistently. NAS 410 sets minimum requirements for qualifying and certifying Level 1, Level 2, Level 3 and Senior Level 3 personnel performing NDT, NDI or NDE in the aerospace manufacturing, service, maintenance and overhaul industries. Revision 6 was released by AIA and Accuris on 1 December 2025 and introduces a new Appendix D creating an additional pathway to Level 3 qualification, under which Level 2 personnel complete designated NDT activities that earn points toward qualification. EN 4179 is technically equivalent as published; the 2026 edition superseded EN 4179:2021 and carries annexes on the Level 3 recertification credit system, Level 1-limited personnel, and NANDTB requirements. Personnel certified to earlier revisions need not recertify until their current certification expires.

NAS 410 Rev 5 (2020) scope and the four levels (Level 1, 2, 3, Senior Level 3) from standard catalogue records. NAS 410 paragraph 4.5 'Responsible Level 3' wording quoted from ndt.net technical forum discussion citing the standard text; treat the paragraph number as indicative and confirm against Rev 6. EN 4179:2021 (BS/DS editions) and EN 4179:2026, listed by BSI and DIN distributors as the current edition published 2026, superseding EN 4179:2021 — verified through distributor catalogue listings rather than the CEN portal. FAA/EASA harmonisation and technical equivalence of EN 4179 and NAS 410 from published NDT qualification literature and the FAA's NDT memorandum for production approval holders. facets.q: Who does NAS 410 / EN 4179 apply to?
facets.a: NDT providers and in-house NDT functions serving aerospace manufacturing, maintenance, repair and overhaul — engine and airframe shops, casting and forging suppliers, and independent NDT houses on aerospace approved-supplier lists. Primes flow the requirement down through purchase orders, and Nadcap audits it under AC7114. Firms selling into both US and European aerospace supply chains have to satisfy the NAS 410 and EN 4179 halves consistently.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for NAS 410 / EN 4179 compliance?
facets.a: Yes. NAS 410 / EN 4179 accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a NAS 410 / EN 4179 audit ask for?
facets.a: Written practice for the training, qualification and certification of NDT personnel, approved by the Responsible Level 3, Written designation of the Responsible Level 3, plus that person's Level 3 certification records and evidence of knowledge of the employer's codes and specifications, Individual qualification files: training, experience, General, Specific and Practical examination results, and vision test records, Documented determination by the Responsible Level 3 — or by a NANDTB where one applies — of the adequacy and equivalency of experience carried in from a prior employer or programme, NDT procedures and work instructions for each method and technique, approved by the Responsible Level 3. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is NAS 410 / EN 4179 renewed?
facets.a: Personnel certification expiry is set by the employer's written practice; NAS 410 states that personnel certified to previous revisions of NAS 410 or EN 4179 need not recertify to the requirements of the new revision until their current certification expires. The company-level cycle is separate and defined by Nadcap: the first reaccreditation audit falls within twelve months of the initial audit, after which the Supplier Merit Program can extend the interval to 18 or 24 months depending on audit performance. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common NAS 410 / EN 4179 findings?
facets.a: Self-audit not performed, or performed without all applicable job audits — consistently among the most-cited AC7114 nonconformances, Required pre-audit package not sent to the auditor 30 days before the audit, Corrective actions from the previous Nadcap audit no longer implemented at the following audit, Calibration requirements not flowed down to subcontracted calibration or subcontracted NDT services. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does NAS 410 / EN 4179 cover?
facets.a: PT, MT, UT, PAUT, RT (film), RT-D / digital radiography, ET. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under NAS 410 / EN 4179
paragraphs: Employer-based, with a named accountable individual. The employer shall identify in writing a Responsible Level 3 to act on its behalf in matters regarding the NDT qualification and certification process; that person shall be certified as a Level 3 in one or more NDT methods and shall have thorough knowledge of the written instructions, codes, specifications and standards the employer uses. NAS 410 does not require an ASNT NDT Level III certificate, though an employer's written practice may accept one as evidence of the General examination. Contracting the Responsible Level 3 role to an outside agency is common and workable — but only the employer certifies personnel, and in Europe a NANDTB may need to approve the Level 3.

facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: Who signs the written practice for NAS 410 / EN 4179?

facets.q: How does a NAS 410 / EN 4179 auditor test this document?

facets.q: What must a corrective action records contain under NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: It has to satisfy NAS 410 / EN 4179 as Aerospace Industries Association (AIA) publishes NAS 410, distributed through Accuris. EN 4179 is prepared by ASD-STAN and published through CEN. Enforcement is by the airframe and engine primes through purchase-order flow-down, by the Performance Review Institute (PRI) through Nadcap audits to AC7114, and by aviation regulators — the FAA treats personnel qualified under EN 4179 as technically equivalent to NAS 410. National Aerospace NDT Boards (NANDTBs) operate in countries that have established them. enforces it: what the firm did about previous findings, which is the first thing a repeat auditor opens. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the corrective action records for NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: The management representative. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a NAS 410 / EN 4179 auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must NAS 410 / EN 4179 records be kept?
facets.a: Personnel certification expiry is set by the employer's written practice; NAS 410 states that personnel certified to previous revisions of NAS 410 or EN 4179 need not recertify to the requirements of the new revision until their current certification expires. The company-level cycle is separate and defined by Nadcap: the first reaccreditation audit falls within twelve months of the initial audit, after which the Supplier Merit Program can extend the interval to 18 or 24 months depending on audit performance. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a NAS 410 / EN 4179 audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: Self-audit not performed, or performed without all applicable job audits — consistently among the most-cited AC7114 nonconformances

facets.q: Does NAS 410 / EN 4179 require a separate procedure for PT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a PT procedure under NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in PT. Because NAS 410 / EN 4179 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover PT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What PT records does a NAS 410 / EN 4179 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's PT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — penetrant, developer, cleaner and emulsifier batch records, plus the light meters for the inspection environment. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common PT finding at audit?
facets.a: Batch certificates missing for consumables used, or dwell time not recorded. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under NAS 410 / EN 4179 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform PT under NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does PT need under NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do PT requirements differ from the other methods in NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. NAS 410 / EN 4179 also covers MT, UT, PAUT, RT (film), RT-D / digital radiography, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

facets.q: Does NAS 410 / EN 4179 require a separate procedure for PAUT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a PAUT procedure under NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in PAUT. Because NAS 410 / EN 4179 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover PAUT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What PAUT records does a NAS 410 / EN 4179 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's PAUT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — the phased array unit, wedges, encoders, and the calibration blocks used for wedge delay, sensitivity and TCG. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common PAUT finding at audit?
facets.a: Data acquired outside the scan plan the procedure qualified, or encoder position not recorded. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under NAS 410 / EN 4179 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform PAUT under NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does PAUT need under NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do PAUT requirements differ from the other methods in NAS 410 / EN 4179?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. NAS 410 / EN 4179 also covers PT, MT, UT, RT (film), RT-D / digital radiography, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

Contracting the Responsible Level 3 role to an outside agency is common and workable — but only the employer certifies personnel, and in Europe a NANDTB may need to approve the Level 3.

title: ISO 9712 Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Inspection service providers bidding work where the client specification names ISO 9712, EN ISO 9712 or a national identical adoption instead of an employer-based.
h1: ISO 9712 Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Inspection service providers bidding work where the client specification names ISO 9712, EN ISO 9712 or a national identical adoption instead of an employer-based scheme — international EPCs, offshore and marine, export fabrication, and Canadian and Brazilian work where the national scheme is effectively mandatory. Personnel certification is central or third-party here, so the firm cannot certify its own technicians internally.
expansion: Because it certifies individuals, it constrains who can be put on a crew, not what the firm's paperwork says. ISO 9712 specifies requirements for the qualification and certification of personnel who perform industrial non-destructive testing. The fifth edition, ISO 9712:2021, was published in December 2021 and cancels and replaces ISO 9712:2012, which it technically revised — clarifying responsibilities for the certification body, authorized qualification body, examination centre and employer, revising training and industrial experience durations, modifying visual acuity testing, adding requirements for renewal candidates, and revising the structured credit system for Level 3 recertification. Its Scope notes that it specifies requirements for what are in effect third-party conformity assessment schemes. For a service provider this changes the shape of a bid: certificates belong to certification bodies and to individuals, not to the company.
source: ISO 9712:2021 itself, fifth edition, 2021-12, read from the ISO-published preview: title page, Foreword (ISO/TC 135/SC 7 with CEN/TC 138 under the Vienna Agreement; fifth edition cancels and replaces the fourth edition ISO 9712:2012; the listed technical changes), Introduction, Clause 1 Scope with its ten methods and NOTE 3 on third-party conformity assessment, Clause 2 normative references (ISO/IEC 17024:2012 and ISO 18490:2015), Clause 3 definitions including 3.11 employer, 3.13 examination centre and 3.20 job-specific training leading to operating authorizations, and the full table of contents (Clauses 5–13, Annexes A–G). Validity period, renewal window and the 12-month recertification rule from European Accreditation's published FAQ on ISO 9712. Canada: Natural Resources Canada NDT certification pages — CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2022 (ISO 9712:2021, IDT), Rules of Implementation, the statement that adoption does not provide full harmonisation or mutual recognition by default, and NDTCB's statement that it retains and does not delegate certification decisions; also NRCan's 2026 notice that CGSB publishing changes do not interrupt NDTCB services. Brazil: ABENDI SNQC-END, accredited by Inmetro as a personnel certification body (OPC-02) to ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 17024 on the criteria of ABNT NBR ISO 9712, operating norm NA-001. United States: ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (ISO 9712:2021):2023 per asnt.org. Note on the normative reference: ISO 9712:2021 cites ISO/IEC 17024:2012 as a dated reference, while ISO/IEC 17024:2026 was published on 1 April 2026 — ANAB has published transition milestones of 1 October 2027 for certification body self-attestation, assessments from October 2027 to September 2028, and 31 March 2029 as the final deadline. Checked August 2026.

facets.q: Who does ISO 9712 apply to?
facets.a: Inspection service providers bidding work where the client specification names ISO 9712, EN ISO 9712 or a national identical adoption instead of an employer-based scheme — international EPCs, offshore and marine, export fabrication, and Canadian and Brazilian work where the national scheme is effectively mandatory. Because it certifies individuals, it constrains who can be put on a crew, not what the firm's paperwork says.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for ISO 9712 compliance?
facets.a: Not for the certification itself. ISO 9712 requires central or third-party personnel certification, so technicians are certified by the scheme rather than by the employer. A consulting Level III still adds value on procedures, documentation, gap assessment and audit attendance — but cannot substitute for the scheme's own certification.

facets.q: What documents does a ISO 9712 audit ask for?
facets.a: Application to the certification body or authorized qualification body naming method, level and industrial or product sector (Annex A), Documented training from a source the certification body recognises, meeting the durations in Clause 7.2, Employer-attested industrial NDT experience performed under supervision in the method and sector (Clause 7.3), Vision evidence meeting Clause 7.4 — near vision acuity and colour vision, with ISO 18490 as the normative reference for evaluating visual acuity, Examination results for the general, specific, practical and NDT instruction writing elements at Levels 1 and 2, or the basic and main method elements at Level 3 (Clause 8). Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is ISO 9712 renewed?
facets.a: Certificates carry a defined validity period, with renewal handled under Clause 10 and recertification under Clause 11. European Accreditation states that ISO 9712 certificates expire at the end of a maximum period of validity of five years, that renewal may be applied for up to 12 months after the expiry date, and that an application for recertification made more than 12 months after expiry requires a complete examination. Where the standard allows latitude, the certification body has the final decision, so the operative numbers come from the scheme rules, not from a universal figure. In the Americas: ASNT 9712 certificates run five years; Canada operates CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2022 (ISO 9712:2021, IDT) with its own Rules of Implementation; Brazil's SNQC-END operates under ABENDI's NA-001. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common ISO 9712 findings?
facets.a: Bidding an ISO 9712 scope with employer-based SNT-TC-1A certificates and assuming they will be accepted, Certificate sector under Annex A does not match the work — a sector-limited certificate used across pre-service and in-service scopes, Certificate lapsed and the renewal window missed, converting a renewal into a complete re-examination, No employer operating authorization on file, so a validly certified technician still cannot be shown as authorised for the client's product. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does ISO 9712 cover?
facets.a: AT — acoustic emission testing, ET — eddy current testing, LT — leak testing (hydraulic pressure tests excluded), MT — magnetic testing, PT — penetrant testing, RT — radiographic testing, ST — strain gauge testing, TT — thermographic testing. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under ISO 9712
paragraphs: Central, third-party — the opposite pole from SNT-TC-1A. The certificate is issued by a certification body, which under the standard's own normative reference to ISO/IEC 17024 must be a properly constituted certification body, and that body retains authority over granting, maintaining, recertification, scope extension, suspension and withdrawal. Canada's NDTCB states plainly that it does not delegate those decisions. An outsourced Level III cannot sign for the firm here. What the employer keeps is real but different: verifying eligibility, delivering job-specific training on its own products, equipment, procedures and codes, and issuing the resulting operating authorization that lets a certified person work.

sections.heading: The audit sequence
items: Select a certification body accredited to ISO/IEC 17024 for the ISO 9712 scheme — or the national identical adoption the client actually names, since adoptions are not automatically interchangeable
Submit application and eligibility evidence: training duration, supervised industrial experience by sector, and vision (Clause 7)

Sit the examinations at an examination centre approved by the certification body — general, specific, practical and instruction writing elements at Levels 1 and 2; basic and main method elements at Level 3 (Clause 8)
Certification decision taken by the certification body alone (Clause 9); the certification body owns the certificate and controls suspension and withdrawal
Employer delivers job-specific training and issues the operating authorization before the person works on the employer's products
Renew under Clause 10 before expiry; recertify under Clause 11, using the Annex C structured credit system where the scheme allows it for renewal at Levels 1, 2 and 3 and for Level 3 recertification

sections.heading: Documents an auditor asks for
items: Application to the certification body or authorized qualification body naming method, level and industrial or product sector (Annex A)
Documented training from a source the certification body recognises, meeting the durations in Clause 7.2
Employer-attested industrial NDT experience performed under supervision in the method and sector (Clause 7.3)
Vision evidence meeting Clause 7.4 — near vision acuity and colour vision, with ISO 18490 as the normative reference for evaluating visual acuity
Examination results for the general, specific, practical and NDT instruction writing elements at Levels 1 and 2, or the basic and main method elements at Level 3 (Clause 8)
The certificate issued by the certification body, showing scope and expiry (Clause 9.2)
The employer's written operating authorization, issued after job-specific training on the employer's products and procedures
Renewal and recertification file, including Annex C structured credit system records where that route is used

sections.heading: Findings firms get against ISO 9712
items: Bidding an ISO 9712 scope with employer-based SNT-TC-1A certificates and assuming they will be accepted
Certificate sector under Annex A does not match the work — a sector-limited certificate used across pre-service and in-service scopes
Certificate lapsed and the renewal window missed, converting a renewal into a complete re-examination
No employer operating authorization on file, so a validly certified technician still cannot be shown as authorised for the client's product
Vision evidence required of certificate holders under Clause 7.4 not maintained by the employer between examinations

Assuming reciprocity between national adoptions — NRCan states that adopting ISO 9712:2021 as CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2022 synchronises the published standards but does not by itself provide full harmonisation or mutual recognition of other certification schemes
Practical examination technique on the certificate narrower than the technique the job actually requires
Certification body chosen whose ISO/IEC 17024 accreditation does not cover the ISO 9712 scheme, or does not cover the specific method

facets.q: How long must ISO 9712 records be kept?

facets.q: What must a records retention schedule contain under ISO 9712?
facets.a: It has to satisfy ISO 9712 as ISO Technical Committee ISO/TC 135, Non-destructive testing, Subcommittee SC 7, Personnel qualification, in collaboration with CEN/TC 138 under the Vienna Agreement. Operationally the authority is the certification body running the scheme, which must operate to ISO/IEC 17024. In the Americas: ASNT Certification Services LLC (ASNT 9712 / ANSI/ASNT CP-9712) in the United States; Natural Resources Canada's National NDT Certification Body (NDTCB) under CAN/CGSB-48.9712 in Canada; ABENDI's SNQC-END, accredited by Inmetro, in Brazil. enforces it: how long each record is kept, where, and who can retrieve it during an audit. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the records retention schedule for ISO 9712?
facets.a: The QA manager. This regime requires central or third-party certification, so the signature works alongside the scheme rather than substituting for it.

facets.q: How does a ISO 9712 auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must ISO 9712 records be kept?
facets.a: Certificates carry a defined validity period, with renewal handled under Clause 10 and recertification under Clause 11. European Accreditation states that ISO 9712 certificates expire at the end of a maximum period of validity of five years, that renewal may be applied for up to 12 months after the expiry date, and that an application for recertification made more than 12 months after expiry requires a complete examination. Where the standard allows latitude, the certification body has the final decision, so the operative numbers come from the scheme rules, not from a universal figure. In the Americas: ASNT 9712 certificates run five years; Canada operates CAN/CGSB-48.9712-2022 (ISO 9712:2021, IDT) with its own Rules of Implementation; Brazil's SNQC-END operates under ABENDI's NA-001. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy ISO 9712?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a ISO 9712 audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: Bidding an ISO 9712 scope with employer-based SNT-TC-1A certificates and assuming they will be accepted

sections.heading: Personnel certification context
paragraphs: Central, third-party — the opposite pole from SNT-TC-1A. The certificate is issued by a certification body, which under the standard's own normative reference to ISO/IEC 17024 must be a properly constituted certification body, and that body retains authority over granting, maintaining, recertification, scope extension, suspension and withdrawal. Canada's NDTCB states plainly that it does not delegate those decisions. An outsourced Level III cannot sign for the firm here. What the employer keeps is real but different: verifying eligibility, delivering job-specific training on its own products, equipment, procedures and codes, and issuing the resulting operating authorization that lets a certified person work.

description: NDT and inspection service providers that issue statements of conformity rather than raw measurements — in-service inspection, third-party witness and shop surveilla
h1: ISO/IEC 17020 Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: NDT and inspection service providers that issue statements of conformity rather than raw measurements — in-service inspection, third-party witness and shop surveillance, field and rope-access crews, and firms bidding public or regulated work that requires accredited inspection. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: It fits providers whose product is a judgement about an item, and it is the standard clients name when they want the provider's independence proven rather than asserted. ISO/IEC 17020 contains requirements for the competence and impartiality of bodies performing inspection and for the consistent operation of their inspection activities. The third edition, ISO/IEC 17020:2026, was published in March 2026 and cancels and replaces the 2012 second edition. The headline change for an inspection firm is that the categorisation of independence collapses from types A, B and C to type A and type non-A, with the independence requirements sitting in normative Annex A and impartiality requirements applying equally to both types. The edition also adds definitions of item and client, adds a subclause on control of data and information and on actions to address risks and opportunities, incorporates the common CASCO elements, and replaces some prescriptive requirements with performance-based ones.

facets.q: Who does ISO/IEC 17020 apply to?
facets.a: NDT and inspection service providers that issue statements of conformity rather than raw measurements — in-service inspection, third-party witness and shop surveillance, field and rope-access crews, and firms bidding public or regulated work that requires accredited inspection. It fits providers whose product is a judgement about an item, and it is the standard clients name when they want the provider's independence proven rather than asserted.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for ISO/IEC 17020 compliance?
facets.a: Yes. ISO/IEC 17020 accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a ISO/IEC 17020 audit ask for?
facets.a: Management system documentation under Clause 8 — policies and responsibilities, documented information, records control, Independence declaration and type A / type non-A justification against normative Annex A, supported by the actual ownership and commercial relationships, Impartiality risk register with evidence of ongoing monitoring of activities and of personnel relationships (4.1.3), and top management commitment to impartiality (4.1.5), Legally enforceable confidentiality commitments extending to employees, contractors, committee members and anyone acting on the body's behalf (4.2.1, 4.2.4), Legal entity evidence and arrangements covering liabilities arising from operations (5.2). Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is ISO/IEC 17020 renewed?
facets.a: ISO/IEC 17020 sets no accreditation interval of its own — the accreditation body's cycle governs, with surveillance assessments between reassessments. What is fixed is the edition deadline. Accreditation bodies have announced a three-year transition from the publication of ISO/IEC 17020:2026, with UKAS and ANAB citing 27 March 2029 as the point after which only accreditation to the 2026 edition is recognised. Existing ISO/IEC 17020:2012-based accreditations remain valid until then, and the main work is re-justifying independence under the type A / type non-A model and evidencing ongoing impartiality risk monitoring. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common ISO/IEC 17020 findings?
facets.a: Independence type asserted without an Annex A justification that matches actual ownership, group companies and commercial relationships — the type A / type non-A change makes previously comfortable type B and C claims worth re-arguing, Impartiality threats identified once at implementation and never monitored on an ongoing basis, including the relationships of personnel (4.1.3), Inspector remuneration linked to inspection outcomes or pass rates, which 4.1.7 treats as a direct nonconformity, Confidentiality commitments not legally enforceable, or not extended to contractors and personnel of external bodies (4.2.4), or the client not informed in advance of information the body intends to make public (4.2.1). These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does ISO/IEC 17020 cover?
facets.a: RT, MT, UT, PAUT, PT, ET, VT, Neutron radiography. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under ISO/IEC 17020
paragraphs: ISO/IEC 17020 names no personnel certification scheme. Clause 6.1 requires the body to define competence criteria and to select, train, authorise and monitor personnel against them; the inspection scheme or the client's specification decides what evidence counts, and Clause 3.3 notes that an inspection scheme can specify independence requirements. In most industrial NDT work an employer-based SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 programme satisfies clause 6.1, which means an outsourced Level III can hold the technical authority — writing competence criteria, approving procedures, signing qualifications. Where the scheme itself demands ISO 9712 certificates, clause 6.1 inherits that requirement and the outsourced Level III can no longer substitute for it.

facets.q: How long does ISO/IEC 17020 audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the ISO/IEC 17020 audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a ISO/IEC 17020 finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does ISO/IEC 17020 require a pre-audit or gap assessment?

facets.q: Who signs the ndt procedures for ISO/IEC 17020?
facets.a: The Level III who approves them. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How long must ISO/IEC 17020 records be kept?

sections.heading: Personnel certification context
paragraphs: ISO/IEC 17020 names no personnel certification scheme. Clause 6.1 requires the body to define competence criteria and to select, train, authorise and monitor personnel against them; the inspection scheme or the client's specification decides what evidence counts, and Clause 3.3 notes that an inspection scheme can specify independence requirements. In most industrial NDT work an employer-based SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 programme satisfies clause 6.1, which means an outsourced Level III can hold the technical authority — writing competence criteria, approving procedures, signing qualifications. Where the scheme itself demands ISO 9712 certificates, clause 6.1 inherits that requirement and the outsourced Level III can no longer substitute for it.

facets.q: What must a corrective action records contain under ISO/IEC 17020?
facets.a: It has to satisfy ISO/IEC 17020 as Developed by the ISO Committee on Conformity Assessment (CASCO) in collaboration with CEN/CLC/JTC 1. Enforced by accreditation bodies — in the United States by ANAB (which runs a dedicated NDE inspection body programme), A2LA (which covers NDT under both ISO/IEC 17020 and ISO/IEC 17025), IAS and PJLA. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the corrective action records for ISO/IEC 17020?
facets.a: The management representative. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a ISO/IEC 17020 auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must ISO/IEC 17020 records be kept?
facets.a: ISO/IEC 17020 sets no accreditation interval of its own — the accreditation body's cycle governs, with surveillance assessments between reassessments. What is fixed is the edition deadline. Accreditation bodies have announced a three-year transition from the publication of ISO/IEC 17020:2026, with UKAS and ANAB citing 27 March 2029 as the point after which only accreditation to the 2026 edition is recognised. Existing ISO/IEC 17020:2012-based accreditations remain valid until then, and the main work is re-justifying independence under the type A / type non-A model and evidencing ongoing impartiality risk monitoring. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy ISO/IEC 17020?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a ISO/IEC 17020 audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: Independence type asserted without an Annex A justification that matches actual ownership, group companies and commercial relationships — the type A / type non-A change makes previously comfortable type B and C claims worth re-arguing

sections.heading: Personnel certification context
paragraphs: ISO/IEC 17020 names no personnel certification scheme. Clause 6.1 requires the body to define competence criteria and to select, train, authorise and monitor personnel against them; the inspection scheme or the client's specification decides what evidence counts, and Clause 3.3 notes that an inspection scheme can specify independence requirements. In most industrial NDT work an employer-based SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 programme satisfies clause 6.1, which means an outsourced Level III can hold the technical authority — writing competence criteria, approving procedures, signing qualifications. facets.q: Does ISO/IEC 17020 require a separate procedure for RT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a RT procedure under ISO/IEC 17020?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in RT. Because ISO/IEC 17020 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover RT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What RT records does a ISO/IEC 17020 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's RT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — source or tube, exposure devices, film or detectors, densitometers, IQIs and the survey meters used to control the area. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common RT finding at audit?
facets.a: IQI sensitivity not achieved, or radiation area control records missing for the shot. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under ISO/IEC 17020 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform RT under ISO/IEC 17020?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does RT need under ISO/IEC 17020?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do RT requirements differ from the other methods in ISO/IEC 17020?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. ISO/IEC 17020 also covers MT, UT, PAUT, PT, ET, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

facets.q: Does ISO/IEC 17020 require a separate procedure for PAUT?

facets.q: Who can approve a PAUT procedure under ISO/IEC 17020?

paragraphs: ISO/IEC 17020 names no personnel certification scheme. title: ISO/IEC 17025 Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: NDT service providers that report measured test results rather than conformity judgements — fixed laboratories, mobile and field crews reporting thickness, hardness
h1: ISO/IEC 17025 Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: NDT service providers that report measured test results rather than conformity judgements — fixed laboratories, mobile and field crews reporting thickness, hardness and flaw data, and firms calibrating their own NDT instruments and reference standards. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: It is also the route for providers whose customers want method-by-method proof of competence and traceable calibration instead of a company-level quality certificate, and for firms that need a scope of accreditation to name specific ASME, AWS or AISC provisions. ISO/IEC 17025:2017, the third edition, sets general requirements for the competence, impartiality and consistent operation of laboratories. It is structured as general requirements covering impartiality and confidentiality, then structural, resource, process and management system requirements, with Clause 8 offering Option A — a set of built-in management system requirements — or Option B, an ISO 9001-conforming system. For an NDT provider the practical consequence is that accreditation is granted method by method: the scope of accreditation names each technique rather than asserting general competence. facets.q: Who does ISO/IEC 17025 apply to?
facets.a: NDT service providers that report measured test results rather than conformity judgements — fixed laboratories, mobile and field crews reporting thickness, hardness and flaw data, and firms calibrating their own NDT instruments and reference standards. It is also the route for providers whose customers want method-by-method proof of competence and traceable calibration instead of a company-level quality certificate, and for firms that need a scope of accreditation to name specific ASME, AWS or AISC provisions.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for ISO/IEC 17025 compliance?
facets.a: Yes. ISO/IEC 17025 accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a ISO/IEC 17025 audit ask for?
facets.a: Management system documentation under Clause 8, Option A or Option B, including control of management system documents and control of records, Scope of accreditation request — for NDT under A2LA, the F215 Scope of Accreditation Selection List, broken down technique by technique, Completed ASTM E1359 self-assessment checklist, submitted to the assessor before the assessment, where the laboratory elects to be assessed to ASTM E543, Test methods and NDT procedures with evidence of selection, verification and validation (7.2), Equipment records and calibration certificates meeting the accreditation body's traceability policy — under A2LA P102 this specifically covers MT ammeters, timers, gauss meters and white/black light meters; RT density film strips; PT pressure gauges, white/black light meters and temperature gauges; VT white light meters; leak test pressure gauges and gas sensing units. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is ISO/IEC 17025 renewed?
facets.a: ISO/IEC 17025 sets no accreditation interval of its own; the accreditation body's cycle governs. A2LA opens renewal assessments seven months before the expiry date with initial documents due six months prior, opens surveillance assessments on the same lead times against the anniversary date, and opens annual reviews four months before with documents due three months before — and proficiency testing documentation is required at initial, renewal, surveillance and annual review alike. Unlike ISO/IEC 17020 and ISO/IEC 17024, which were both reissued in 2026, ISO/IEC 17025:2017 remains the current edition, so there is no edition transition to plan for. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common ISO/IEC 17025 findings?
facets.a: Equipment and reference measurement standards without calibration records meeting the accreditation body's traceability policy — A2LA reports that around 38% of its nonconformances fall under clause 6.4, Externally provided products and services not evaluated or controlled — A2LA reports around 21% of nonconformances under clause 6.6, concentrated in 6.6.2, Management review outputs missing the records required by clause 8.9.3, Date of issue omitted from test reports, against clause 7.8.2.1 j). These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does ISO/IEC 17025 cover?
facets.a: PT — visible, fluorescent, RT — X-ray (digital and/or film), gamma (digital and/or film), MT — prod, yoke and bench, visible or fluorescent, wet or dry, UT — contact straight beam, contact angle beam, immersion straight beam, immersion angle beam, immersion phased array, ET, VT, LT — pressure drop, gas detection, gas concentration, flow rate, AE. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under ISO/IEC 17025
paragraphs: ISO/IEC 17025 requires competence but prescribes no certification scheme. Clause 6.2 requires documented competence requirements plus procedures and records for selecting, training, supervising, authorising and monitoring personnel — and clause 6.2.5 is a recurring deficiency in published A2LA assessment data. An employer-based SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 programme satisfies it, so an outsourced Level III can own the competence criteria, approve the NDT procedures and authorise technicians, and a laboratory can be accredited without a single third-party-certified individual. facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the ISO/IEC 17025 audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a ISO/IEC 17025 finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does ISO/IEC 17025 require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first ISO/IEC 17025 audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the personnel certification records for ISO/IEC 17025?
facets.a: The QA manager. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a ISO/IEC 17025 auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must ISO/IEC 17025 records be kept?
facets.a: ISO/IEC 17025 sets no accreditation interval of its own; the accreditation body's cycle governs. A2LA opens renewal assessments seven months before the expiry date with initial documents due six months prior, opens surveillance assessments on the same lead times against the anniversary date, and opens annual reviews four months before with documents due three months before — and proficiency testing documentation is required at initial, renewal, surveillance and annual review alike. Unlike ISO/IEC 17020 and ISO/IEC 17024, which were both reissued in 2026, ISO/IEC 17025:2017 remains the current edition, so there is no edition transition to plan for. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy ISO/IEC 17025?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.
