CSA Z662 is revised on a roughly four-year cycle — 1994, 1996, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2011, 2015, 2019, 2023 — and Z662:23 is the ninth edition, released 30 June 2023. Because the Onshore Pipeline Regulations incorporate the latest version by reference, a new edition takes effect on publication rather than on an adoption date. The Canada Energy Regulator's Information Advisory IA 2023-001 told companies to review Z662:23 and take the steps needed to comply as soon as possible, and to demonstrate for pending applications how projects would meet the new requirements. There is no certificate to renew under this regime; what expires is the personnel certification behind it and the currency of the procedures written to it.
Applies to the personnel certification behind this method

facets.q: Does CSA Z662 require a separate procedure for UT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a UT procedure under CSA Z662?
facets.a: Approval follows the certification scheme and the governing specification rather than the employer alone. The person approving must hold the scheme's qualification for UT at the appropriate level.

facets.q: What UT records does a CSA Z662 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's UT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, cables, couplant, and the calibration and reference blocks used to set sensitivity. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common UT finding at audit?
facets.a: An in-calibration instrument used with an unidentified or out-of-calibration reference block. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under CSA Z662 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform UT under CSA Z662?
facets.a: Where the scheme's certification travels with the individual, yes — that is the point of central certification. Verify the certificate covers UT at the level required and is current, since scope and expiry are what get checked.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does UT need under CSA Z662?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do UT requirements differ from the other methods in CSA Z662?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. CSA Z662 also covers RT, MT, PT, VT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for UT
paragraphs: Central certification only. Clause 7.14.8.1 requires radiographers to be qualified as specified in CAN/CGSB-48.9712, with radiographic image interpretation at Level 2 or 3; Clause 7.15.6 requires ultrasonic inspectors to be qualified to Level 2 or 3; and confirmation of complete crack removal by liquid penetrant or wet magnetic particle inspection must be by inspectors qualified to the same standard. There is no employer written practice route. This is exactly where an outsourced Level III earns his place: the requirement introduced in Z662:19 and carried into Z662:23 that a CGSB Level 3 review and approve non-destructive inspection procedures is a signature a pipeline contractor can buy in.

h1: NR-13 Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Every Brazilian employer operating boilers above 60 kPa operating pressure, pressure vessels whose P·V product exceeds 8 or which contain class A fluids, interconnecting piping carrying class A or B fluids, and metallic storage tanks over 3 m external diameter and 20,000 litres nominal capacity. Personnel certification is central or third-party here, so the firm cannot certify its own technicians internally.
expansion: Inspection service providers are bound indirectly but absolutely: the employer must be able to prove that every inspection, test and NDT report it buys satisfies NR-13. NR-13 places the legal duty on the employer, not the contractor, and that shapes how inspection service providers sell into Brazil. Every safety inspection must be executed under the technical responsibility of a Profissional Legalmente Habilitado (PLH) — item 13.3.3. Selection of examinations and tests, hydrostatic and pneumatic test procedures, interval extensions and the consolidated report all rest on that PLH's technical judgement, and the report must carry the PLH's legible name, signature and professional-council registration number. A provider supplying only NDT technicians cannot sign; it must employ a Brazil-registered engineer or work under the client's PLH. Metallic storage tanks entered scope on 4 July 2026, opening a substantial new inspection market.

facets.q: Who does NR-13 apply to?
facets.a: Every Brazilian employer operating boilers above 60 kPa operating pressure, pressure vessels whose P·V product exceeds 8 or which contain class A fluids, interconnecting piping carrying class A or B fluids, and metallic storage tanks over 3 m external diameter and 20,000 litres nominal capacity. Inspection service providers are bound indirectly but absolutely: the employer must be able to prove that every inspection, test and NDT report it buys satisfies NR-13.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for NR-13 compliance?
facets.a: Not for the certification itself. NR-13 requires central or third-party personnel certification, so technicians are certified by the scheme rather than by the employer. A consulting Level III still adds value on procedures, documentation, gap assessment and audit attendance — but cannot substitute for the scheme's own certification.

facets.q: What documents does a NR-13 audit ask for?
facets.a: Prontuário da caldeira / prontuário do vaso de pressão — manufacturer's data book, including construction code and edition, material specification, PMTA methodology, fabrication hydrostatic test records, safety-device data and category (items 13.4.1.5 a and 13.5.1.5 a), Registro de Segurança — a numbered-page book, folder set or computerised system recording all occurrences affecting safety, interval changes, and initial, periodic and extraordinary inspections with the equipment's operational condition, Projeto de Instalação — boiler installation design, authored under the responsibility of a PLH (item 13.4.2.1), Projeto de Alteração ou Reparo, Relatórios de Inspeção de Segurança — initial, periodic and extraordinary, with the prescribed minimum content. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is NR-13 renewed?
facets.a: Boilers, periodic internal and external examination (item 13.4.4.4): maximum 12 months for categories A and B; 18 months for alkali recovery boilers of any category; 24 months for category A provided safety valve opening pressures are tested at 12 months; 30 months for category B with a combustion management system meeting Annex IV. Establishments holding a certified SPIE may extend to 24 months (alkali recovery and category B), 30 months (category A) and 48 months (category A with a Safety Instrumented System meeting Annex IV). Pressure vessels follow Table 2 by category I to V — external examination at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 years and internal at 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10 years; with a certified SPIE, external at 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 years and internal at 6, 8, 10 and 12 years, with category V internal at technical criterion. A certified SPIE using a documented risk-based methodology may extend further, capped at 10 years for internal examination of category I vessels. Piping follows the internal interval of the most critical connected vessel or boiler and may be doubled on the PLH's technical justification, capped at 10 years. Boilers reaching 25 years of use undergo a broader integrity assessment at the following inspection. Postponement of up to six months is possible with a risk assessment coordinated by a PLH, and must be formally justified to the predominant workers' union. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common NR-13 findings?
facets.a: Consolidated inspection report signed by an NDT Level III or a senior technician rather than by a PLH — the report content lists require the PLH's legible name, signature and professional-council registration number, Prontuário incomplete or missing the PMTA calculation memory; item 13.4.1.6 requires reconstitution under the technical responsibility of the manufacturer or a PLH, and functional characteristics, safety-device data and the PMTA calculation are non-negotiable, Registro de Segurança that does not record the equipment's operational condition, or lacks the boiler operator's signature alongside the PLH's at the time of inspection (item 13.4.1.8 b), Contracted NDT technicians holding employer-issued or foreign certificates with no SNQC certificate for the method and industrial sector. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does NR-13 cover?
facets.a: VT, UT, UT thickness measurement, PAUT, TOFD, MT, PT, RT. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under NR-13
paragraphs: Two separate requirements, and confusing them is the classic and expensive mistake. The PLH is not an NDT Level III: item 13.3.2 defines it as a person legally competent to practise engineering in Brazil under the prevailing professional regulation, so an ASNT Level III without Brazilian engineering registration cannot sign an NR-13 inspection report. Certification of the PLH's competences is voluntary, through an Organismo de Certificação de Pessoas accredited by Cgcre/Inmetro, with recertification every sixty months (Annex III). For NDT technicians, Annex II requires contracted NDT labour to be certified under prevailing regulation, and Inmetro's SPIE requirements make that ABNT NBR NM ISO 9712 — central third-party certification, not an employer written practice.

sections.heading: The audit sequence
items: Classification — the employer confirms scope under item 13.2.1 and categorises each boiler as A (operating pressure at or above 1,960 kPa) or B (above 60 kPa and below 1,960 kPa) and each pressure vessel into categories I to V.

Initial safety inspection before the equipment enters service at its definitive installation location, comprising internal examination, external examination and a pressure test, under PLH technical responsibility; fabrication-stage hydrostatic testing evidenced by a report signed by a PLH.
Inspection programme and plan drawn up and approved by the PLH, defining the examinations and tests per applicable codes and the equipment's history.

Periodic safety inspections at the maximum intervals of item 13.4.4.4 (boilers) and Table 2 (pressure vessels), with outcomes and operational condition entered in the Registro de Segurança and signed by the PLH and, for boilers, the operator present.
Extraordinary inspection after accidental damage, significant repair or alteration, relocation, or extended idleness (over 12 months for vessels, over 24 months for tanks).

Enforcement — Auditores-Fiscais do Trabalho examine the documentation on site. NR-13 issues no certificate of any kind; the only certificate route is the voluntary SPIE scheme of Annex II, certified by an Inmetro-accredited OCP.

facets.q: How long does NR-13 audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE), which publishes the Normas Regulamentadoras; enforced on site by Auditores-Fiscais do Trabalho look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common NR-13 findings?
facets.a: Consolidated inspection report signed by an NDT Level III or a senior technician rather than by a PLH — the report content lists require the PLH's legible name, signature and professional-council registration number, Prontuário incomplete or missing the PMTA calculation memory; item 13.4.1.6 requires reconstitution under the technical responsibility of the manufacturer or a PLH, and functional characteristics, safety-device data and the PMTA calculation are non-negotiable, Registro de Segurança that does not record the equipment's operational condition, or lacks the boiler operator's signature alongside the PLH's at the time of inspection (item 13.4.1.8 b), Contracted NDT technicians holding employer-issued or foreign certificates with no SNQC certificate for the method and industrial sector. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the NR-13 audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a NR-13 finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does NR-13 require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first NR-13 audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: How long must NR-13 records be kept?

facets.q: Does NR-13 require a separate procedure for VT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a VT procedure under NR-13?
facets.a: Approval follows the certification scheme and the governing specification rather than the employer alone. The person approving must hold the scheme's qualification for VT at the appropriate level.

facets.q: What VT records does a NR-13 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's VT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — light meters, measuring aids, mirrors and borescopes where remote viewing is used. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common VT finding at audit?
facets.a: Illumination at the surface never measured, or near-vision acuity test lapsed. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under NR-13 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform VT under NR-13?
facets.a: Where the scheme's certification travels with the individual, yes — that is the point of central certification. Verify the certificate covers VT at the level required and is current, since scope and expiry are what get checked.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does VT need under NR-13?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do VT requirements differ from the other methods in NR-13?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. NR-13 also covers UT, UT thickness measurement, PAUT, TOFD, MT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

facets.q: How do RT requirements differ from the other methods in NR-13?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. NR-13 also covers VT, UT, UT thickness measurement, PAUT, TOFD, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for RT
paragraphs: Two separate requirements, and confusing them is the classic and expensive mistake. The PLH is not an NDT Level III: item 13.3.2 defines it as a person legally competent to practise engineering in Brazil under the prevailing professional regulation, so an ASNT Level III without Brazilian engineering registration cannot sign an NR-13 inspection report. Certification of the PLH's competences is voluntary, through an Organismo de Certificação de Pessoas accredited by Cgcre/Inmetro, with recertification every sixty months (Annex III). For NDT technicians, Annex II requires contracted NDT labour to be certified under prevailing regulation, and Inmetro's SPIE requirements make that ABNT NBR NM ISO 9712 — central third-party certification, not an employer written practice.

facets.q: Who does SNQC (ABENDI) apply to?
facets.a: Individual NDT practitioners rather than firms — but it binds firms hard, because Inmetro's SPIE requirements, Petrobras fabrication inspection specifications and most Brazilian industrial buyers all demand SNQC-certified technicians. Any inspection service provider staffing work in Brazil, including a foreign firm mobilising a crew for a turnaround, must field individually SNQC-certified people in the specific method, level and industrial sector concerned.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for SNQC (ABENDI) compliance?
facets.a: Not for the certification itself. SNQC (ABENDI) requires central or third-party personnel certification, so technicians are certified by the scheme rather than by the employer. A consulting Level III still adds value on procedures, documentation, gap assessment and audit attendance — but cannot substitute for the scheme's own certification.

facets.q: What documents does a SNQC (ABENDI) audit ask for?
facets.a: Certificado SNQC for each technician, stating the method, level, sublevel where applicable, and industrial sector, Formulário de solicitação de certificação — the application lodged with ABENDI for a specific method, level and sector, Comprovação de treinamento — training records evidencing hours per method and level, Comprovação de experiência industrial, attested by the employer for the method and level claimed, Atestado de acuidade visual — near-vision and colour-contrast examination records. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is SNQC (ABENDI) renewed?
facets.a: ABENDI publishes that certification at any of the three levels is valid for sixty months, after which recertification is required. The scheme follows ISO 9712's structure, in which continued validity depends on maintaining satisfactory vision records and continuity of activity in the method. Do not quote a recertification route — examination versus a documented structured-credit path — to a client without reading the current NA-001 revision, which has been revised many times and had reached at least Rev 34; ABENDI announced in February 2023 that SNQC was being updated to align with the new ISO 9712 edition, the first in roughly ten years. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common SNQC (ABENDI) findings?
facets.a: Technician holds a valid SNQC certificate for a different industrial sector than the work performed — steel-sector certification used on refinery pressure equipment is the classic case, Phased array or TOFD performed by a technician holding only a general ultrasonic certificate with no corresponding sublevel, NDT procedures approved by a Level III whose SNQC certification has lapsed, or who holds only ASNT credentials, Vision examination records stale, or missing the colour-contrast assessment. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does SNQC (ABENDI) cover?
facets.a: US — ultrasonic testing, with sublevels including thickness measurement, welds, forgings, laminates, phased array and TOFD, ER — radiographic testing, LP — liquid penetrant, PM — magnetic particle, EV — visual, CP — eddy current, EA — acoustic emission, LT — leak testing. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under SNQC (ABENDI)
paragraphs: Central, third-party certification — the single most important fact for anyone selling outsourced Level III services into Brazil. ABENDI issues the certificate as an accredited personnel certification body operating to ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 17024; the employer certifies nobody, and an SNT-TC-1A written practice signed by a contracted Level III carries no standing in the scheme. facets.q: How long does SNQC (ABENDI) audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does ABENDI — Associação Brasileira de Ensaios Não Destrutivos e Inspeção, acting as an Organismo de Certificação de Pessoas (OPC) accredited by the Coordenação Geral de Acreditação (Cgcre) of Inmetro look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common SNQC (ABENDI) findings?
facets.a: Technician holds a valid SNQC certificate for a different industrial sector than the work performed — steel-sector certification used on refinery pressure equipment is the classic case, Phased array or TOFD performed by a technician holding only a general ultrasonic certificate with no corresponding sublevel, NDT procedures approved by a Level III whose SNQC certification has lapsed, or who holds only ASNT credentials, Vision examination records stale, or missing the colour-contrast assessment. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the SNQC (ABENDI) audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a SNQC (ABENDI) finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does SNQC (ABENDI) require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first SNQC (ABENDI) audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

Do not quote a recertification route — examination versus a documented structured-credit path — to a client without reading the current NA-001 revision, which has been revised many times and had reached at least Rev 34; ABENDI announced in February 2023 that SNQC was being updated to align with the new ISO 9712 edition, the first in roughly ten years. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy SNQC (ABENDI)?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a SNQC (ABENDI) audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: Technician holds a valid SNQC certificate for a different industrial sector than the work performed — steel-sector certification used on refinery pressure equipment is the classic case

sections.heading: Personnel certification context
paragraphs: Central, third-party certification — the single most important fact for anyone selling outsourced Level III services into Brazil. ABENDI issues the certificate as an accredited personnel certification body operating to ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 17024; the employer certifies nobody, and an SNT-TC-1A written practice signed by a contracted Level III carries no standing in the scheme. An outsourced Level III can still write and approve procedures, train candidates and act as a firm's technical authority, but only if that individual personally holds a valid SNQC Level 3 in the relevant method and sector. Foreign ASNT or PCN credentials do not convert automatically; the individual sits SNQC examinations.

answer: Inspection bodies, testing and calibration laboratories, and certification bodies operating in Brazil. Personnel certification is central or third-party here, so the firm cannot certify its own technicians internally.
expansion: Two routes matter to an NDT service provider: accreditation as an Organismo de Inspeção Acreditado under ISO/IEC 17020, where Inmetro maintains a specific non-destructive testing scope; and, for an industrial end user's in-house inspection department, certification of a Serviço Próprio de Inspeção de Equipamentos (SPIE) under NR-13's Annex II, whose conformity assessment requirements Inmetro writes and owns. facets.q: Who does Inmetro / Cgcre apply to?
facets.a: Inspection bodies, testing and calibration laboratories, and certification bodies operating in Brazil. Two routes matter to an NDT service provider: accreditation as an Organismo de Inspeção Acreditado under ISO/IEC 17020, where Inmetro maintains a specific non-destructive testing scope; and, for an industrial end user's in-house inspection department, certification of a Serviço Próprio de Inspeção de Equipamentos (SPIE) under NR-13's Annex II, whose conformity assessment requirements Inmetro writes and owns.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for Inmetro / Cgcre compliance?
facets.a: Not for the certification itself. Inmetro / Cgcre requires central or third-party personnel certification, so technicians are certified by the scheme rather than by the employer. A consulting Level III still adds value on procedures, documentation, gap assessment and audit attendance — but cannot substitute for the scheme's own certification.

facets.q: What documents does a Inmetro / Cgcre audit ask for?
facets.a: Solicitação formal de certificação to the OCP, with a detailed description of the establishment, its location, general layout and the geographic distribution of operating units (SPIE clause 6.2), Information on activities performed by third parties and outsourced installations capable of affecting the certification, including equipment connected to SPIE equipment, Types and quantities of equipment controlled, NR-13 classification, available human resources with their locations, functions and competences, Programa e plano de inspeção, with evidence of minimum compliance with the programme, Procedimentos escritos for the principal activities performed. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is Inmetro / Cgcre renewed?
facets.a: SPIE certificates are valid for 48 months from issue (clause 6.2.5.3). Maintenance audits run every 12 months from the certificate date. That may be extended to 18 months only where all four conditions hold: certified for at least two certification cycles; no suspension in the last two cycles; no warning in the last cycle; and no Category A non-conformities in the last cycle. The extension takes effect only from the start of the cycle following the request and can be revoked at any time following a major accident, a warning or a suspension. Recertification must be concluded before the current certificate expires. Portaria Inmetro nº 62/2026 revokes Portarias Inmetro nº 537/2015, nº 582/2015, nº 177/2023 and nº 382/2023 twelve months after it takes effect; certificates already issued are updated to reference it at the next evaluation stage, and adoption of INI or a Safety Instrumented System by a certified SPIE requires a specific-scope audit. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common Inmetro / Cgcre findings?
facets.a: Contracted NDT reports annexed to the consolidated inspection report but neither referenced nor technically validated by the responsible PLH, contrary to the SPIE reporting rule, No documented criteria for evaluating the performance of contracted inspection services, or no records of those evaluations (clause 9.2), Inspection equipment list incomplete, or calibration not traceable to nationally or internationally recognised standards with no documented and periodically reviewed alternative basis (clause 10.5), Repeated delays in executing the inspection plan detected across successive audit cycles. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does Inmetro / Cgcre cover?
facets.a: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under Inmetro / Cgcre
paragraphs: Inmetro does not certify NDT people; it accredits the bodies that do, under ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 17024, which is how ABENDI's SNQC acquires its legal weight. In the SPIE requirements consolidated by Portaria Inmetro nº 62/2026, clause 5.1.3.11 a requires NDT inspectors to hold the qualification and certification of ABNT NBR NM ISO 9712, welding inspectors ABNT NBR 14842 and painting inspectors ABNT NBR 15218. Employer-issued certification is not accepted for those roles. Clause 5.1.3.12 is the only relief valve: for NDT methods not covered by national standards, an international qualification or documented formal training from the manufacturer or technology owner may be required instead.

items: Formal application to an Organismo de Certificação de Produtos (OCP) established in Brazil and accredited by Inmetro, submitting the establishment description, equipment inventory and resource information.

Initial audit planning — the OCP builds the audit plan, verifies the inspection programme including any overdue items, and defines the sample; the workforce (efetivo) is verified and the checklist prepared.
On-site initial audit against the checklist, with the inspection programme assessed in full and the remaining requirements assessed by sampling.

Certificate of Conformity issued, valid 48 months from the date of issue.

Maintenance audits every 12 months from certificate issue, and recertification concluded before the certificate expires — planned like a maintenance audit but decided under the initial-evaluation rules.

facets.q: How long does Inmetro / Cgcre audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Inmetro, a federal body under the Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços; accreditation is performed by its Coordenação Geral de Acreditação (Cgcre), described by Inmetro as the only accreditation body recognised by the Brazilian government look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common Inmetro / Cgcre findings?
facets.a: Contracted NDT reports annexed to the consolidated inspection report but neither referenced nor technically validated by the responsible PLH, contrary to the SPIE reporting rule, No documented criteria for evaluating the performance of contracted inspection services, or no records of those evaluations (clause 9.2), Inspection equipment list incomplete, or calibration not traceable to nationally or internationally recognised standards with no documented and periodically reviewed alternative basis (clause 10.5), Repeated delays in executing the inspection plan detected across successive audit cycles. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the Inmetro / Cgcre audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a Inmetro / Cgcre finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does Inmetro / Cgcre require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first Inmetro / Cgcre audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: What must a equipment calibration records contain under Inmetro / Cgcre?
facets.a: It has to satisfy Inmetro / Cgcre as Inmetro, a federal body under the Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços; accreditation is performed by its Coordenação Geral de Acreditação (Cgcre), described by Inmetro as the only accreditation body recognised by the Brazilian government enforces it: the traceable evidence that every instrument was in calibration on the day it was used. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the equipment calibration records for Inmetro / Cgcre?
facets.a: The equipment custodian. This regime requires central or third-party certification, so the signature works alongside the scheme rather than substituting for it.

facets.q: How does a Inmetro / Cgcre auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must Inmetro / Cgcre records be kept?
facets.a: SPIE certificates are valid for 48 months from issue (clause 6.2.5.3). Maintenance audits run every 12 months from the certificate date. That may be extended to 18 months only where all four conditions hold: certified for at least two certification cycles; no suspension in the last two cycles; no warning in the last cycle; and no Category A non-conformities in the last cycle. The extension takes effect only from the start of the cycle following the request and can be revoked at any time following a major accident, a warning or a suspension. Recertification must be concluded before the current certificate expires. Portaria Inmetro nº 62/2026 revokes Portarias Inmetro nº 537/2015, nº 582/2015, nº 177/2023 and nº 382/2023 twelve months after it takes effect; certificates already issued are updated to reference it at the next evaluation stage, and adoption of INI or a Safety Instrumented System by a certified SPIE requires a specific-scope audit. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy Inmetro / Cgcre?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a Inmetro / Cgcre audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: Contracted NDT reports annexed to the consolidated inspection report but neither referenced nor technically validated by the responsible PLH, contrary to the SPIE reporting rule

facets.q: Does Inmetro / Cgcre require a separate procedure for UT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a UT procedure under Inmetro / Cgcre?
facets.a: Approval follows the certification scheme and the governing specification rather than the employer alone. The person approving must hold the scheme's qualification for UT at the appropriate level.

facets.q: What UT records does a Inmetro / Cgcre audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's UT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, cables, couplant, and the calibration and reference blocks used to set sensitivity. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common UT finding at audit?
facets.a: An in-calibration instrument used with an unidentified or out-of-calibration reference block. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under Inmetro / Cgcre is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform UT under Inmetro / Cgcre?
facets.a: Where the scheme's certification travels with the individual, yes — that is the point of central certification. Verify the certificate covers UT at the level required and is current, since scope and expiry are what get checked.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does UT need under Inmetro / Cgcre?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do UT requirements differ from the other methods in Inmetro / Cgcre?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. Inmetro / Cgcre also covers PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

title: Petrobras cadastro / RQT Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Companies wanting to supply goods or services to Petrobras — fabrication shops, inspection contractors and NDT service providers among them.
h1: Petrobras cadastro / RQT Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Companies wanting to supply goods or services to Petrobras — fabrication shops, inspection contractors and NDT service providers among them. Personnel certification is central or third-party here, so the firm cannot certify its own technicians internally.
expansion: It also reaches down the chain: the general fabrication inspection specification applies to direct and indirect purchases whose final client is Petrobras, so a subcontractor two tiers down still inherits the personnel certification rules, and it applies to goods families carrying a Requisito de Qualificação Técnica in the Petrobras register. Petrobras publishes far more than most national oil companies, which makes this regime unusually researchable. Supplier registration is documented publicly on the Canal Fornecedor, and Petrobras technical specifications and N-series standards are downloadable from the public Petronect content area without a contract. The commercially decisive document for inspection providers is ET-0000.00-0000-972-P8L-001, 'Requisito Geral de Inspeção de Fabricação', which sets minimum fabrication inspection requirements for direct and indirect purchases destined for Petrobras. What Petrobras does not publish is the internal scoring, weighting and thresholds behind supplier evaluation, so nothing should be claimed about how a bid is actually ranked — a distinction worth making explicitly to any client who asks.
source: Petrobras specification ET-0000.00-0000-972-P8L-001, 'Requisito Geral de Inspeção de Fabricação', Rev. B, dated 20 October 2016 (Rev. A 19 September 2016, Rev. 0 10 November 2015), downloaded from the public Petronect content area and extracted; sections 1 (Objetivo), 2 (Referências), 6 and 7 (Qualificação e Certificação de Pessoal) and 8 (Planejamento da Inspeção de Fabricação) read directly. Supplier registration process, the named evaluation dimensions (legal, economic-financial, technical, SMS, Due Diligence de Integridade), the certificado de registro cadastral, pre-qualification, the Regulamento de Licitações e Contratos and the Catálogo de Padronização from Petrobras's public Canal Fornecedor at canalfornecedor.petrobras.com.br. Petrobras N-1594, N-1595, N-1596, N-1597 and N-1598 titles taken from the specification's own reference list, not from those standards themselves — note in particular that N-1595 is the radiography standard, not a personnel standard. Limitation: I-ET-0000.00-0000-970-PSQ-001 is named in clause 7 but was not retrievable (404 on Petronect), so the alternative qualification route it defines is not characterised here. Verified 21 August 2026.

facets.q: Who does Petrobras cadastro / RQT apply to?
facets.a: Companies wanting to supply goods or services to Petrobras — fabrication shops, inspection contractors and NDT service providers among them. It also reaches down the chain: the general fabrication inspection specification applies to direct and indirect purchases whose final client is Petrobras, so a subcontractor two tiers down still inherits the personnel certification rules, and it applies to goods families carrying a Requisito de Qualificação Técnica in the Petrobras register.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for Petrobras cadastro / RQT compliance?
facets.a: Not for the certification itself. Petrobras cadastro / RQT requires central or third-party personnel certification, so technicians are certified by the scheme rather than by the employer. A consulting Level III still adds value on procedures, documentation, gap assessment and audit attendance — but cannot substitute for the scheme's own certification.

facets.q: What documents does a Petrobras cadastro / RQT audit ask for?
facets.a: Cadastro submission on Petronect, with the questionnaire of general and commercial company information and the products and services offered, Certificado de registro cadastral, issued on successful registration and documented as a distinct component of the supplier programme, Requisito de Qualificação Técnica (RQT) evidence for each goods family being registered, Plano de Inspeção e Testes (PIT), prepared by the supplier to cover all production, installation and associated service processes of the supply, Termo de adequação do procedimento de inspeção por ensaios não destrutivos. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is Petrobras cadastro / RQT renewed?
facets.a: Petrobras documents the certificado de registro cadastral as a component of the supplier programme and treats registration as something the supplier must keep current. Petrobras does not publish a single fixed validity for technical qualification applicable across all goods families, so no interval should be quoted to a client without checking the specific Requisito de Qualificação Técnica for that family. On the technical side the operative rule is edition control rather than renewal: the specification states that the edition or revision of applicable documents is the one in force at the date of contract signature. Personnel certificates renew on their own scheme's cycle — sixty months for SNQC. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common Petrobras cadastro / RQT findings?
facets.a: NDT technicians presented with ASNT or other employer-based certificates where clause 7 requires SNQC certification, with no evidence of meeting the I-ET-0000.00-0000-970-PSQ-001 alternative, PIT that does not cover all production, installation and associated service processes of the supply, or that omits the additional inspection requirements defined for the goods family, NDT procedures used without the termo de adequação that the specification requires, Standard editions applied that are not those in force at the date of contract signature. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does Petrobras cadastro / RQT cover?
facets.a: UT — Petrobras N-1594 covers ultrasonic testing of welds, RT — Petrobras N-1595, PT — Petrobras N-1596, VT — Petrobras N-1597, MT — Petrobras N-1598, Dimensional control inspection (ABNT NBR 15523), Welding inspection (ABNT NBR 14842), Painting inspection (ABNT NBR 15218). Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

facets.q: How long does Petrobras cadastro / RQT audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Petróleos Brasileiros S.A. (Petrobras) as the contracting party; registration administered through the Canal Fornecedor and the Petronect portal, with technical requirements issued as Petrobras N-series standards and ET / I-ET specifications look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common Petrobras cadastro / RQT findings?
facets.a: NDT technicians presented with ASNT or other employer-based certificates where clause 7 requires SNQC certification, with no evidence of meeting the I-ET-0000.00-0000-970-PSQ-001 alternative, PIT that does not cover all production, installation and associated service processes of the supply, or that omits the additional inspection requirements defined for the goods family, NDT procedures used without the termo de adequação that the specification requires, Standard editions applied that are not those in force at the date of contract signature. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the Petrobras cadastro / RQT audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a Petrobras cadastro / RQT finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does Petrobras cadastro / RQT require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first Petrobras cadastro / RQT audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: What must a ndt procedures contain under Petrobras cadastro / RQT?
facets.a: It has to satisfy Petrobras cadastro / RQT as Petróleos Brasileiros S.A. (Petrobras) as the contracting party; registration administered through the Canal Fornecedor and the Petronect portal, with technical requirements issued as Petrobras N-series standards and ET / I-ET specifications enforces it: the method-specific instructions technicians actually work to, and the approval that makes them valid. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the ndt procedures for Petrobras cadastro / RQT?
facets.a: The Level III who approves them. This regime requires central or third-party certification, so the signature works alongside the scheme rather than substituting for it.

facets.q: How does a Petrobras cadastro / RQT auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must Petrobras cadastro / RQT records be kept?
facets.a: Petrobras documents the certificado de registro cadastral as a component of the supplier programme and treats registration as something the supplier must keep current. Petrobras does not publish a single fixed validity for technical qualification applicable across all goods families, so no interval should be quoted to a client without checking the specific Requisito de Qualificação Técnica for that family. On the technical side the operative rule is edition control rather than renewal: the specification states that the edition or revision of applicable documents is the one in force at the date of contract signature. Personnel certificates renew on their own scheme's cycle — sixty months for SNQC. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy Petrobras cadastro / RQT?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a Petrobras cadastro / RQT audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. title: NOM-020-STPS Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Every workplace in Mexican national territory operating pressure vessels, cryogenic vessels, steam generators or boilers, with named exclusions including diving bell
h1: NOM-020-STPS Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Every workplace in Mexican national territory operating pressure vessels, cryogenic vessels, steam generators or boilers, with named exclusions including diving bells, hyperbaric chambers, fire extinguishers, portable compressed-gas cylinders, LPG vessels regulated by the energy ministry and rail tank cars. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: The commercial market for an inspection provider is Category II and III equipment, which carries mandatory periodic pressure testing or non-destructive examination. The current designation is confirmed: NOM-020-STPS-2011, published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación on 27 December 2011 and in force from 27 June 2012, superseding NOM-020-STPS-2002, with an authorised alternative procedure published 9 December 2014 and continued validity confirmed by systematic review on 15 August 2022. It is the engine of the Mexican NDT inspection market because it makes periodic non-destructive examination or pressure testing mandatory rather than discretionary for Category II and III equipment. The employer classifies each item into Category I, II or III from fluid hazard, relief-device set pressure and volume, maintains a per-equipment file, and either contracts an accredited inspection unit or — for Category III only — constitutes its own Type B unit.

facets.q: What are the most common NOM-020-STPS findings?

paragraphs: Clause 4.21 defines 'personal certificado' as a person with the technical capability and experience to perform, supervise, interpret and evaluate NDT results in accordance with NMX-B-482-1991, or the standards that replace it, or an equivalent. items: Classify each item into Category I, II or III per clause 7 and Table 1, using the set pressure of the relief device, the volume, and whether the fluid is hazardous.

facets.q: How long does NOM-020-STPS audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social (STPS); conformity assessed by unidades de inspección (statutory term until 2020: unidades de verificación) that are accredited by an accreditation entity and approved by STPS look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common NOM-020-STPS findings?
facets.a: Equipment misclassified into Category I or II to escape the Category III duties to have a unidad de inspección present and to notify STPS, Only a volumetric examination performed, with no accompanying surface or flux-loss examination as clause 13.5 requires, NDT results endorsed by a technician whose certification cannot be traced to NMX-B-482, its replacement, or a demonstrably equivalent scheme, Pressure test endorsed by an NDT technician rather than by an engineer with knowledge in the matter, contrary to clause 13.2 f and i. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the NOM-020-STPS audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a NOM-020-STPS finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does NOM-020-STPS require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first NOM-020-STPS audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: What must a examination records contain under NOM-020-STPS?
facets.a: It has to satisfy NOM-020-STPS as Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social (STPS); conformity assessed by unidades de inspección (statutory term until 2020: unidades de verificación) that are accredited by an accreditation entity and approved by STPS enforces it: the general, specific and practical examination papers and results behind each certification. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the examination records for NOM-020-STPS?
facets.a: The employer's Level III. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a NOM-020-STPS auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must NOM-020-STPS records be kept?
facets.a: For Category II and III equipment: the first pressure test or NDT is due before ten years from the manufacturing certificate or code stamp for new equipment that has one; equipment without that certificate or stamp, and all used equipment, is tested before entering service. Thereafter at least every five years, performed within the sixty calendar days before the end of each five-year period. The periodicity is determined by the employer's qualified personnel and may in no case exceed five years (clause 13.2 a). Dictámenes issued by a unidad de inspección are valid ten years for new equipment and five years for used equipment (clause 19.7). Boilers additionally require functional testing of safety shutdowns. Category III equipment requires a notice to STPS within sixty days of the dictamen. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy NOM-020-STPS?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a NOM-020-STPS audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. facets.q: How long does ema audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does ema, operating as an Entidad de Acreditación under the Ley de Infraestructura de la Calidad; sectoral aprobación is granted separately by the regulating dependency — for pressure equipment under NOM-020, the Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common ema findings?
facets.a: Type declared as A while the unit also inspects for a related party, breaching the independence conditions that type requires, Competence criteria for inspectors written generically rather than per inspection activity and method, with no authorisation records tying a named inspector to a specific scope, Metrological traceability gaps — calibration certificates without traceability to recognised standards, or equipment in use past its calibration date, Testificación allowed to lapse beyond four years from the last witnessed inspection. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the ema audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a ema finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does ema require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first ema audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

title: Pemex proveedores / NRF Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Companies bidding for or supplying goods and services to Pemex, including inspection and NDT contractors and the fabrication shops they serve.
h1: Pemex proveedores / NRF Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Companies bidding for or supplying goods and services to Pemex, including inspection and NDT contractors and the fabrication shops they serve. Personnel certification is central or third-party here, so the firm cannot certify its own technicians internally.
expansion: Registration in the padrón de proveedores y contratistas is documented as a precondition for participating in Pemex's open bidding, and the technical requirements flow down to subcontractors through the standards the contract cites. Pemex publishes more than most national oil companies. The padrón de proveedores y contratistas is a public registry described on pemex.com, and the Normas de Referencia (NRF) and the newer PEMEX-EST technical standards are published as downloadable PDFs on the same site, issued by the Comité de Normalización de Petróleos Mexicanos y Organismos Subsidiarios and applied as mandatory in Pemex acquisitions and service contracting. facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Petróleos Mexicanos (Pemex); technical standards issued by the Comité de Normalización de Petróleos Mexicanos y Organismos Subsidiarios look at first?

facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's UT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, cables, couplant, and the calibration and reference blocks used to set sensitivity. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common UT finding at audit?
facets.a: An in-calibration instrument used with an unidentified or out-of-calibration reference block. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under Pemex proveedores / NRF is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform UT under Pemex proveedores / NRF?
facets.a: Where the scheme's certification travels with the individual, yes — that is the point of central certification. Verify the certificate covers UT at the level required and is current, since scope and expiry are what get checked.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does UT need under Pemex proveedores / NRF?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do UT requirements differ from the other methods in Pemex proveedores / NRF?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. Pemex proveedores / NRF also covers PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for UT
paragraphs: This is where Pemex diverges sharply from baseline Mexican practice, and it is the argument that sells. NOM-020 accepts 'personal certificado' under NMX-B-482 or an equivalent, which leaves room for an employer written practice; published Pemex reference standards are stricter, requiring NDT personnel to be qualified and certified to ISO 9712 or to NMX-B-482-CANACERO-2016, with ISO 11484 cited as the applicable route for certain steel-product scopes, which follows a different qualification model. Level rules apply: Level 1 works only under direct Level 2 supervision, and interpretation of results is issued by Level 3, or by Level 2 with Level 3 approval. An outsourced Level III must personally hold certification under the scheme the contract cites.

facets.q: Who does IRAM / OAA apply to?
facets.a: Any inspection or NDT service provider working in Argentina on gas transmission and distribution pipelines regulated by ENARGAS, on refinery and petrochemical plant, on Vaca Muerta oilfield fabrication and gathering lines, on nuclear facilities, or on structural and pressure fabrication where the client cites IRAM standards. facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for IRAM / OAA compliance?
facets.a: Not for the certification itself. IRAM / OAA requires central or third-party personnel certification, so technicians are certified by the scheme rather than by the employer. A consulting Level III still adds value on procedures, documentation, gap assessment and audit attendance — but cannot substitute for the scheme's own certification.

facets.q: What documents does a IRAM / OAA audit ask for?
facets.a: Certificados de calificación IRAM-NM-ISO 9712, Nivel 1, 2 or 3, per method, showing issuing body and expiry date, Registro de agudeza visual: near vision and colour differentiation, dated within the last twelve months, Procedimientos escritos de END, calificados y documentados, signed by an inspector competent to IRAM NM ISO 9712, per NAG-100 Section 243 b)(1), Registros de Calificación de Procedimientos (RCP/PQR) issued by an Ente Habilitado per IRAM/IAS U 500-138, or by a welding inspector certified per IRAM/IAS U 500-169, Certificados de Inspector de Soldadura per IRAM/IAS U 500-169 for the visual inspection required by NAG-100 Section 241. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is IRAM / OAA renewed?
facets.a: IRAM-NM-ISO 9712 is the Argentine adoption of the Mercosur standard NM ISO 9712, whose April 2025 edition is an identical adoption of ISO 9712:2021 and whose previous edition, January 2014, adopted ISO 9712:2012. On that basis the ISO 9712 cycle applies: certificates run five years, are renewed once on evidence of continued visual acuity and uninterrupted activity, and require recertification at ten years. Confirm which edition IRAM has adopted before quoting an exam route. OAA accreditation is maintained by periodic surveillance and reassessment; OAA does not publish the interval on its public pages, so verify it in the current OAA rules rather than assuming a number. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common IRAM / OAA findings?
facets.a: NDT procedures on file are unsigned, or are signed by someone whose Level III certificate does not cover the method the procedure addresses, contrary to NAG-100 Section 243 b)(1), Technicians hold only an employer-issued SNT-TC-1A card with no IRAM-NM-ISO 9712 certificate, and the auditor treats the whole method scope as uncovered for regulated pipeline work, Certificates expired but technicians still on the job roster; no system tracking the five-year expiry against crew assignment, Annual visual acuity records missing, or older than twelve months, for personnel on active assignment. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does IRAM / OAA cover?
facets.a: UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, Thickness measurement (ME). Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

paragraphs: Central and third-party, not employer-based. facets.q: How long does IRAM / OAA audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Instituto Argentino de Normalización y Certificación (IRAM) as certification body; Organismo Argentino de Acreditación (OAA) as the sole national accreditation body; Ente Nacional Regulador del Gas (ENARGAS) as the sector regulator for gas transmission and distribution look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common IRAM / OAA findings?
facets.a: NDT procedures on file are unsigned, or are signed by someone whose Level III certificate does not cover the method the procedure addresses, contrary to NAG-100 Section 243 b)(1), Technicians hold only an employer-issued SNT-TC-1A card with no IRAM-NM-ISO 9712 certificate, and the auditor treats the whole method scope as uncovered for regulated pipeline work, Certificates expired but technicians still on the job roster; no system tracking the five-year expiry against crew assignment, Annual visual acuity records missing, or older than twelve months, for personnel on active assignment. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the IRAM / OAA audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a IRAM / OAA finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does IRAM / OAA require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first IRAM / OAA audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting.
