description: What IRAM / OAA requires for Phased Array Ultrasonics: procedure approval, personnel qualification, equipment evidence and what an auditor samples.
h1: Phased Array Ultrasonics (PAUT) Requirements Under IRAM / OAA
answer: Procedure qualification usually requires a demonstration on a representative flawed sample, and the scan plan forms part of the approved procedure rather than a field decision. IRAM / OAA, enforced by Instituto Argentino de Normalización y Certificación (IRAM) as certification body; Organismo Argentino.: Central and third-party, not employer-based.
expansion: An auditor examining PAUT asks for the phased array unit, wedges, encoders, and the calibration blocks used for wedge delay, sensitivity and TCG. Argentina issues no single NDT licence. Two things bind a service provider. First, personnel: technicians are expected to hold certification to IRAM-NM-ISO 9712, the Argentine adoption of the Mercosur standard NM ISO 9712, issued by an accredited certification body rather than by their own employer. Second, where the work is regulated the regulator names that standard directly. ENARGAS NAG-100 Part E, Section 243, requires NDT of pipeline welds to be carried out by persons trained and certified at Level 2 or 3 to IRAM NM ISO 9712 or recognised equivalent international standards, and requires the written, qualified NDT procedures to be signed by an inspector competent to the same standard. A firm selling inspection as an accredited third party additionally pursues OAA accreditation under IRAM-ISO/IEC 17020.
source: IRAM, NDT operators certification scheme page (accessed August 2026), stating IRAM-NM-ISO 9712, IRAM-ISO/IEC 17024 and OAA accreditation since 2004; CNEA Departamento de Ensayos No Destructivos y Estructurales OCA page (methods and levels: US, PM, CI, LP, RI levels 1-3, USPA levels 1-2) and INTI Organismo de Certificación pages citing IRAM-ISO/IEC 17024, NM ISO 9712 and IRAM 710, and OAA persons-certification scope reference OCH-003 (accessed August 2026); ENARGAS NAG-100 Año 1993, Adenda N.º 3 Año 2026, Parte E, Sections 221, 225, 227, 229, 241, 243 and 245, text read directly, approved by ENARGAS Resolución 62/2026 published in the Boletín Oficial on 10 February 2026 and effective 11 February 2026, which also repeals NAG-105; AMN/Mercosur catalogue record for NM ISO 9712, April 2025 edition, identical adoption of ISO 9712:2021, superseding the January 2014 edition; OAA public site (accessed August 2026), noting Decreto 1474/94 as the framework for the Sistema Nacional de Normas, Calidad y Certificación, and the replacement of ILAC and IAF by Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated (GLOBAC) from 1 January 2026.

IRAM-NM-ISO 9712 is the Argentine adoption of the Mercosur standard NM ISO 9712, whose April 2025 edition is an identical adoption of ISO 9712:2021 and whose previous edition, January 2014, adopted ISO 9712:2012. On that basis the ISO 9712 cycle applies: certificates run five years, are renewed once on evidence of continued visual acuity and uninterrupted activity, and require recertification at ten years. Confirm which edition IRAM has adopted before quoting an exam route. OAA accreditation is maintained by periodic surveillance and reassessment; OAA does not publish the interval on its public pages, so verify it in the current OAA rules rather than assuming a number.
Applies to the personnel certification behind this method

facets.q: Does IRAM / OAA require a separate procedure for PAUT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a PAUT procedure under IRAM / OAA?
facets.a: Approval follows the certification scheme and the governing specification rather than the employer alone. The person approving must hold the scheme's qualification for PAUT at the appropriate level.

facets.q: What PAUT records does a IRAM / OAA audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's PAUT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — the phased array unit, wedges, encoders, and the calibration blocks used for wedge delay, sensitivity and TCG. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common PAUT finding at audit?
facets.a: Data acquired outside the scan plan the procedure qualified, or encoder position not recorded. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under IRAM / OAA is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform PAUT under IRAM / OAA?
facets.a: Where the scheme's certification travels with the individual, yes — that is the point of central certification. Verify the certificate covers PAUT at the level required and is current, since scope and expiry are what get checked.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does PAUT need under IRAM / OAA?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do PAUT requirements differ from the other methods in IRAM / OAA?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. IRAM / OAA also covers UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for PAUT
paragraphs: Central and third-party, not employer-based. IRAM operates an OAA-accredited scheme under IRAM-ISO/IEC 17024, accredited since 2004, certifying to IRAM-NM-ISO 9712; examinations are delivered by IRAM-authorised qualifying bodies (Organismos de Calificación Autorizados) including CNEA's OCA and UTN Facultad Regional Delta. INTI runs a separate OAA-accredited certification body for persons, scope reference OCH-003, using NM ISO 9712 and IRAM 710. An employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice does not on its own produce a certificate Argentina recognises for ENARGAS-regulated work. An outsourced Level III can still sign procedures under NAG-100's "normas equivalentes internacionales reconocidas" wording where he holds a centrally issued certificate such as ASNT NDT Level III.

IRAM-NM-ISO 9712 is the Argentine adoption of the Mercosur standard NM ISO 9712, whose April 2025 edition is an identical adoption of ISO 9712:2021 and whose previous edition, January 2014, adopted ISO 9712:2012. On that basis the ISO 9712 cycle applies: certificates run five years, are renewed once on evidence of continued visual acuity and uninterrupted activity, and require recertification at ten years. Confirm which edition IRAM has adopted before quoting an exam route. OAA accreditation is maintained by periodic surveillance and reassessment; OAA does not publish the interval on its public pages, so verify it in the current OAA rules rather than assuming a number.
Applies to the personnel certification behind this method

facets.q: Does IRAM / OAA require a separate procedure for ET?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a ET procedure under IRAM / OAA?
facets.a: Approval follows the certification scheme and the governing specification rather than the employer alone. The person approving must hold the scheme's qualification for ET at the appropriate level.

facets.q: What ET records does a IRAM / OAA audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's ET certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, and the reference standards carrying the notches or holes used to set the response. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common ET finding at audit?
facets.a: Reference standard not representative of the material or geometry examined. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under IRAM / OAA is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform ET under IRAM / OAA?
facets.a: Where the scheme's certification travels with the individual, yes — that is the point of central certification. Verify the certificate covers ET at the level required and is current, since scope and expiry are what get checked.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does ET need under IRAM / OAA?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do ET requirements differ from the other methods in IRAM / OAA?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. IRAM / OAA also covers UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for ET
paragraphs: Central and third-party, not employer-based. IRAM operates an OAA-accredited scheme under IRAM-ISO/IEC 17024, accredited since 2004, certifying to IRAM-NM-ISO 9712; examinations are delivered by IRAM-authorised qualifying bodies (Organismos de Calificación Autorizados) including CNEA's OCA and UTN Facultad Regional Delta. INTI runs a separate OAA-accredited certification body for persons, scope reference OCH-003, using NM ISO 9712 and IRAM 710. An employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice does not on its own produce a certificate Argentina recognises for ENARGAS-regulated work. An outsourced Level III can still sign procedures under NAG-100's "normas equivalentes internacionales reconocidas" wording where he holds a centrally issued certificate such as ASNT NDT Level III.

title: INN / SICEP Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: NDT and inspection contractors serving Chilean copper, lithium and gold mines, concentrator plants, smelters, ports and the pulp, power and refining sectors.
h1: INN / SICEP Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: NDT and inspection contractors serving Chilean copper, lithium and gold mines, concentrator plants, smelters, ports and the pulp, power and refining sectors. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: It binds any firm bidding into Codelco, BHP, Antofagasta Minerals and comparable operators, any firm inspecting boilers, autoclaves and steam equipment, and any firm claiming accredited inspection status inside Chile. Chile does not licence NDT companies. Access is controlled in two separate places instead. Accreditation: INN runs the Sistema Nacional de Acreditación and accredits inspection bodies against NCh-ISO 17020:2012 under its accreditation regulation INN-R401. Accreditation is voluntary in itself but becomes obligatory wherever a technical regulation incorporates it; applications go through INN's SDAC portal on forms F407-21-01 and FD-D06-04, and accreditations are granted for five years, renewable, with surveillance evaluations during the term. Commercial access: the mining majors screen contractors through SICEP, the Sistema de Calificación de Empresas Proveedoras, which rates financial capacity, operational and technical capability, legal and labour compliance and risk prevention. A firm can be technically excellent and still not be biddable without SICEP standing.

facets.q: Who does INN / SICEP apply to?
facets.a: NDT and inspection contractors serving Chilean copper, lithium and gold mines, concentrator plants, smelters, ports and the pulp, power and refining sectors. It binds any firm bidding into Codelco, BHP, Antofagasta Minerals and comparable operators, any firm inspecting boilers, autoclaves and steam equipment, and any firm claiming accredited inspection status inside Chile.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for INN / SICEP compliance?
facets.a: Yes. INN / SICEP accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a INN / SICEP audit ask for?
facets.a: Práctica Escrita to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, signed and dated by the Level III, naming every method, level and technique and the education, training, experience and examination requirements for each, Certificados de calificación y certificación del personal by method and level, with general, specific and practical examination papers and grading records, Registros de agudeza visual (Jaeger N.º 1 or equivalent) and colour differentiation, dated within the last twelve months, Procedimientos de END approved by the Level III and traceable to ASME BPVC Section V, AWS D1.1, API or the client's own specification, Certificados de calibración de equipos plus verification records for reference blocks, transducers and gauges. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is INN / SICEP renewed?
facets.a: INN accreditation is granted for five years and may be renewed for further five-year cycles, with surveillance evaluations during the term to verify continued conformity; INN does not publish a fixed surveillance month on its public pages, so confirm the schedule in INN-R401 rather than assuming one. SICEP standing is a periodically updated diagnosis rather than a fixed-term certificate and lapses if the file is not maintained. Boiler and autoclave inspection under the Ministry of Health regulation runs on a frequency tied to equipment category; establish the category before quoting an interval to a client. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common INN / SICEP findings?
facets.a: The written practice is a generic template that was never tailored to the methods and techniques the company actually sells, and the Level III who signed it is no longer engaged, Level II technicians certified in UT are performing phased array with no separate technique qualification and no documented examination, Vision records missing for technicians on site, or dated more than twelve months before the inspection, Marketing claims "acreditado por el INN" when the INN scope covers only some methods or only one address; INN accreditation is granted against a specific annexed scope and site. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does INN / SICEP cover?
facets.a: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under INN / SICEP
paragraphs: Employer-based certification is accepted, and in practice is the norm. Chile has adopted ISO 9712 as NCh-ISO 9712, but the 2018 edition is shown as no longer current in INN's own catalogue, and INN's register of accredited personnel certification bodies does not list a Chilean body certifying NDT personnel to it, so there is no verified domestic route to an ISO 9712 certificate. Chilean technicians therefore hold employer certification written against ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or ISO 9712 certificates issued by foreign bodies. An outsourced ASNT Level III can write and sign the employer's written practice, approve procedures and certify Level I and II staff, which is how most Chilean NDT firms operate.

facets.q: How long does INN / SICEP audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Instituto Nacional de Normalización (INN), which is both the national standards body and the national accreditation body; Servicio Nacional de Geología y Minería (SERNAGEOMIN) for mine safety; the SEREMI de Salud for boilers, autoclaves and steam equipment; SICEP, administered by the Asociación de Industriales de Antofagasta, as the mining supplier register look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common INN / SICEP findings?
facets.a: The written practice is a generic template that was never tailored to the methods and techniques the company actually sells, and the Level III who signed it is no longer engaged, Level II technicians certified in UT are performing phased array with no separate technique qualification and no documented examination, Vision records missing for technicians on site, or dated more than twelve months before the inspection, Marketing claims "acreditado por el INN" when the INN scope covers only some methods or only one address; INN accreditation is granted against a specific annexed scope and site. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the INN / SICEP audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a INN / SICEP finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does INN / SICEP require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first INN / SICEP audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: Who signs the equipment calibration records for INN / SICEP?

facets.q: How does a INN / SICEP auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: Does INN / SICEP require a separate procedure for UT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a UT procedure under INN / SICEP?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in UT. Because INN / SICEP accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover UT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What UT records does a INN / SICEP audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's UT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, cables, couplant, and the calibration and reference blocks used to set sensitivity. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common UT finding at audit?
facets.a: An in-calibration instrument used with an unidentified or out-of-calibration reference block. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under INN / SICEP is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform UT under INN / SICEP?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does UT need under INN / SICEP?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do UT requirements differ from the other methods in INN / SICEP?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. INN / SICEP also covers PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

facets.q: Does INN / SICEP require a separate procedure for PAUT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. facets.q: Who can approve a PAUT procedure under INN / SICEP?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in PAUT. Because INN / SICEP accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover PAUT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What PAUT records does a INN / SICEP audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's PAUT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — the phased array unit, wedges, encoders, and the calibration blocks used for wedge delay, sensitivity and TCG. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common PAUT finding at audit?
facets.a: Data acquired outside the scan plan the procedure qualified, or encoder position not recorded. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under INN / SICEP is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform PAUT under INN / SICEP?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does PAUT need under INN / SICEP?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. sections.heading: Personnel certification for PAUT
paragraphs: Employer-based certification is accepted, and in practice is the norm. Chile has adopted ISO 9712 as NCh-ISO 9712, but the 2018 edition is shown as no longer current in INN's own catalogue, and INN's register of accredited personnel certification bodies does not list a Chilean body certifying NDT personnel to it, so there is no verified domestic route to an ISO 9712 certificate. title: TOFD Requirements Under INN / SICEP
description: What INN / SICEP requires for Time of Flight Diffraction: procedure approval, personnel qualification, equipment evidence and what an auditor samples.
h1: Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD) Requirements Under INN / SICEP
answer: Coverage is defined by probe separation and depth of field, so a single setup rarely covers full wall thickness and the procedure must state how the remaining zones are examined. facets.a: A Level III qualified in PT. Because INN / SICEP accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover PT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What PT records does a INN / SICEP audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's PT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — penetrant, developer, cleaner and emulsifier batch records, plus the light meters for the inspection environment. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common PT finding at audit?
facets.a: Batch certificates missing for consumables used, or dwell time not recorded. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under INN / SICEP is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform PT under INN / SICEP?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do PT requirements differ from the other methods in INN / SICEP?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. INN / SICEP also covers UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for PT
paragraphs: Employer-based certification is accepted, and in practice is the norm. Chile has adopted ISO 9712 as NCh-ISO 9712, but the 2018 edition is shown as no longer current in INN's own catalogue, and INN's register of accredited personnel certification bodies does not list a Chilean body certifying NDT personnel to it, so there is no verified domestic route to an ISO 9712 certificate. title: INACAL / OSINERGMIN Audit Preparation
description: How a INACAL / OSINERGMIN audit runs, what Instituto Nacional de Calidad (INACAL), Dirección de Acreditación, as the national accreditation body; Organismo Superviso
h1: INACAL / OSINERGMIN Audit Preparation for Inspection Companies
answer: A INACAL / OSINERGMIN audit runs in 7 stages, beginning with file form da-002 with annexes and the fee through inacal's dasgac platform,.. Instituto Nacional de Calidad (INACAL), Dirección de Acreditación, as the national accreditation body; Organismo Supervisor de la Inversión en Energía y Minería (OSINERGMIN) as the energy and mining regulator; Ministerio de Energía y Minas (MINEM) as the rule-maker tests the system by sampling finished work.
expansion: Peru is the clearest regional case of accreditation made compulsory by regulation rather than chosen for marketing. INACAL's Dirección de Acreditación accredits inspection bodies against NTP-ISO/IEC 17020, using application form DA-002 filed through INACAL's management platform, with the fee calculated on the number of procedures in scope. OSINERGMIN then layers a sector registry on top. Under Decreto Supremo N° 001-2022-EM, periodic hermeticity inspection of buried tanks and piping storing liquid fuels and OPDH may only be performed by inspection bodies accredited by INACAL and entered in OSINERGMIN's Registro de Empresas Inspectoras, with the inscription procedure approved by Resolución de Consejo Directivo N° 151-2024-OS/CD. Without both, the certificate the site needs has no standing. What separates firms that clear an audit from firms that collect findings is not the quality of the documentation but whether it describes what actually happens.
source: Ley N° 30224, Ley que crea el Sistema Nacional para la Calidad y el Instituto Nacional de Calidad, published 11 July 2014, with INACAL operational from 1 June 2015 having absorbed INDECOPI's Servicio Nacional de Acreditación, Servicio Nacional de Metrología and the Comisión de Normalización; INACAL accreditation pages including "¿Cómo obtener la Acreditación?" listing form DA-002 for inspection bodies and the DASGAC platform, and the Organismos de Inspección page citing NTP-ISO/IEC 17020, accessed August 2026; OSINERGMIN "Inspección Periódica de Hermeticidad" page citing Decreto Supremo N° 001-2022-EM, which supersedes DS N° 064-2009-EM, and Resolución de Consejo Directivo N° 151-2024-OS/CD, accessed August 2026; the text of the hermeticity norm read directly, including the definitions of Entidad Acreditada and Certificado de Inspección de Hermeticidad, the 0.1 gallons per hour leak index and the thirty-day filing period; OSINERGMIN supervision guidance for LPG direct consumers and distribution networks, version 1.0, May 2022, read directly, citing DS N° 065-2008-EM Article 19, DS N° 001-2007-EM Article 9, NTP 321.123 clauses 5.1.1 to 5.1.15, ASME Section VIII Division 1, API 510 and NB-23; MINEM DS N° 024-2016-EM, Reglamento de Seguridad y Salud Ocupacional en Minería, as modified by DS N° 023-2017-EM and DS N° 034-2023-EM. No NTP adoption of ISO 9712 was found, so none is cited.

INACAL does not publish the accreditation term or the supervision interval on its public accreditation pages, so confirm both in the current accreditation criteria before committing to a client; do not quote a number from another country's practice. What is fixed sits on the regulated side. For buried tank systems, the first hermeticity certificate is required before the system enters service, and thereafter the periodicity is set by the Índice de Riesgo assessment carried out for that specific installation. The inspection report must be submitted to OSINERGMIN within thirty calendar days of the test, and the hermeticity test itself must detect a leak rate of at least 0.1 gallons per hour (0.3785 litres per hour).
Diarised from the certificate date, not the last audit

facets.q: How long does INACAL / OSINERGMIN audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Instituto Nacional de Calidad (INACAL), Dirección de Acreditación, as the national accreditation body; Organismo Supervisor de la Inversión en Energía y Minería (OSINERGMIN) as the energy and mining regulator; Ministerio de Energía y Minas (MINEM) as the rule-maker look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common INACAL / OSINERGMIN findings?
facets.a: The firm holds INACAL accreditation but is not entered in OSINERGMIN's Registro de Empresas Inspectoras, so the hermeticity certificates it issues are rejected on supervision, Accredited scope does not name the specific normative document the client is relying on, so the certificate falls outside scope even though the method itself is covered, Risk-index report and hermeticity report not filed with OSINERGMIN within thirty calendar days of the test, LPG stationary tank accepted on the nameplate alone, with no Certificado de Conformidad from an INACAL-accredited certification body and no U-1 or U-1A data report. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the INACAL / OSINERGMIN audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a INACAL / OSINERGMIN finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does INACAL / OSINERGMIN require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first INACAL / OSINERGMIN audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: Does INACAL / OSINERGMIN require a separate procedure for UT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a UT procedure under INACAL / OSINERGMIN?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in UT. Because INACAL / OSINERGMIN accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover UT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What UT records does a INACAL / OSINERGMIN audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's UT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, cables, couplant, and the calibration and reference blocks used to set sensitivity. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common UT finding at audit?
facets.a: An in-calibration instrument used with an unidentified or out-of-calibration reference block. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under INACAL / OSINERGMIN is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform UT under INACAL / OSINERGMIN?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does UT need under INACAL / OSINERGMIN?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do UT requirements differ from the other methods in INACAL / OSINERGMIN?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. INACAL / OSINERGMIN also covers PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

facets.q: What is the most common RT finding at audit?

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform RT under INACAL / OSINERGMIN?

title: ONAC Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: NDT and inspection contractors in Colombian oil and gas: drill pipe and tubing inspection at pipe yards, tank and pipeline integrity work, and flare-efficiency.
h1: ONAC Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: NDT and inspection contractors in Colombian oil and gas: drill pipe and tubing inspection at pipe yards, tank and pipeline integrity work, and flare-efficiency and leak-detection inspection at production facilities. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: It binds firms selling into the Ecopetrol group, Frontera, Parex, Geopark and the drilling contractors, and any firm that puts an accreditation mark on an inspection report. ONAC is the Colombian state's accreditation body and its inspection body scheme, coded OIN, is where NDT sits. Scopes are granted against ISO/IEC 17020:2012 under inspection field code 22, "Equipos y elementos a través de ensayos no destructivos — END", and the annexed scope names the exact activity, the execution criteria and the acceptance and rejection criteria down to the clause and table, plus the inspection body type A, B or C. Two hydrocarbon inspection scopes have been made effectively compulsory by regulation: flare efficiency measurement and natural gas leak detection and quantification at production facilities, under Ministerio de Minas y Energía Resolución 40066 de 2022 as modified by Resolución 40317 de 2023, and ANH Resolución 10981 de 2023.

facets.q: Who does ONAC apply to?
facets.a: NDT and inspection contractors in Colombian oil and gas: drill pipe and tubing inspection at pipe yards, tank and pipeline integrity work, and flare-efficiency and leak-detection inspection at production facilities. It binds firms selling into the Ecopetrol group, Frontera, Parex, Geopark and the drilling contractors, and any firm that puts an accreditation mark on an inspection report.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for ONAC compliance?
facets.a: Yes. ONAC accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a ONAC audit ask for?
facets.a: Solicitud de acreditación with the proposed scope drafted the way ONAC's annex is drafted: inspection field code, inspection activity, execution criteria, acceptance and rejection criteria, and body type, Internal inspection procedures cited by exact name and version number, in the style of "Ultrasonido — Medición de Espesores con Scan B en Tuberías de perforación (Drill Pipe - Heavy Weight) y tubería de producción (Tubing) V.8", Controlled copies of every normative document named in the scope, at the edition named: DS-1 Drill Stem Inspection Vol. 3 5th ed. 2020, ASME BPVC.V-2023 Article 23 SE-797, API Spec 5CT 11th ed. December 2023, API RP 5C1 8th ed. 2020, API Std 653, Impartiality analysis and the declared type A, B or C under ISO/IEC 17020:2012, Personnel competence records covering certification, authorisation, training, witnessed performance and ongoing monitoring per ISO/IEC 17020 clause 6.1. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is ONAC renewed?
facets.a: ONAC does not run one fixed validity across every scheme; the certificate itself carries the expiry date, and it is the surveillance rhythm that is published. Under the accreditation service rules RAC-3.0-01, version 12 dated 8 January 2025, from the first renewal onwards ONAC schedules surveillance evaluations in months 9, 21, 33 and 45 after approval of the renewal, with re-evaluation in month 55, and the new cycle begins from publication of the certificate in the DOA. A live example: certificate 24-OIN-053 carries a grant date of 28 July 2025 and an expiry of 27 July 2028. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common ONAC findings?
facets.a: Scope creep: the firm inspects a tubular size or applies a normative document that is not in the annexed scope, so the report cannot legitimately carry the accreditation mark, The internal procedure version named in the ONAC annex has been superseded internally without notifying ONAC of the change, Acceptance criteria applied from a different edition than the annex names; DS-1 Volume 3, 5th edition 2020, clause 3.6.5 and tables 3.6.1, 3.6.2 and 3.11.2 are specific, and an older edition's tables are a finding, A type C inspection body performing work that, as contracted, makes it supplier or repairer of the item inspected, breaking the declared impartiality arrangement. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does ONAC cover?
facets.a: UT including B-scan thickness measurement, MFL (magnetic flux leakage), PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT and dimensional inspection, ET. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

title: ONAC Audit Preparation
description: How a ONAC audit runs, what Organismo Nacional de Acreditación de Colombia (ONAC) as the national accreditation body; Ministerio de Minas y Energía and the Agencia N
h1: ONAC Audit Preparation for Inspection Companies
answer: A ONAC audit runs in 6 stages, beginning with submit the application and scope to onac; onac applies its application-review procedure.. Organismo Nacional de Acreditación de Colombia (ONAC) as the national accreditation body; Ministerio de Minas y Energía and the Agencia Nacional de Hidrocarburos (ANH) for the regulated hydrocarbon inspection scopes tests the system by sampling finished work backwards to the records behind it, so preparation means reconciling.
expansion: ONAC is the Colombian state's accreditation body and its inspection body scheme, coded OIN, is where NDT sits. Scopes are granted against ISO/IEC 17020:2012 under inspection field code 22, "Equipos y elementos a través de ensayos no destructivos — END", and the annexed scope names the exact activity, the execution criteria and the acceptance and rejection criteria down to the clause and table, plus the inspection body type A, B or C. Two hydrocarbon inspection scopes have been made effectively compulsory by regulation: flare efficiency measurement and natural gas leak detection and quantification at production facilities, under Ministerio de Minas y Energía Resolución 40066 de 2022 as modified by Resolución 40317 de 2023, and ANH Resolución 10981 de 2023. What separates firms that clear an audit from firms that collect findings is not the quality of the documentation but whether it describes what actually happens.

facets.q: How long does ONAC audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Organismo Nacional de Acreditación de Colombia (ONAC) as the national accreditation body; Ministerio de Minas y Energía and the Agencia Nacional de Hidrocarburos (ANH) for the regulated hydrocarbon inspection scopes look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common ONAC findings?
facets.a: Scope creep: the firm inspects a tubular size or applies a normative document that is not in the annexed scope, so the report cannot legitimately carry the accreditation mark, The internal procedure version named in the ONAC annex has been superseded internally without notifying ONAC of the change, Acceptance criteria applied from a different edition than the annex names; DS-1 Volume 3, 5th edition 2020, clause 3.6.5 and tables 3.6.1, 3.6.2 and 3.11.2 are specific, and an older edition's tables are a finding, A type C inspection body performing work that, as contracted, makes it supplier or repairer of the item inspected, breaking the declared impartiality arrangement. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the ONAC audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a ONAC finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does ONAC require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first ONAC audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: What must a personnel certification records contain under ONAC?
facets.a: It has to satisfy ONAC as Organismo Nacional de Acreditación de Colombia (ONAC) as the national accreditation body; Ministerio de Minas y Energía and the Agencia Nacional de Hidrocarburos (ANH) for the regulated hydrocarbon inspection scopes enforces it: the file proving each technician is currently certified for the work they are doing. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the personnel certification records for ONAC?
facets.a: The QA manager. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a ONAC auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must ONAC records be kept?
facets.a: ONAC does not run one fixed validity across every scheme; the certificate itself carries the expiry date, and it is the surveillance rhythm that is published. Under the accreditation service rules RAC-3.0-01, version 12 dated 8 January 2025, from the first renewal onwards ONAC schedules surveillance evaluations in months 9, 21, 33 and 45 after approval of the renewal, with re-evaluation in month 55, and the new cycle begins from publication of the certificate in the DOA. A live example: certificate 24-OIN-053 carries a grant date of 28 July 2025 and an expiry of 27 July 2028. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy ONAC?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a ONAC audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: Scope creep: the firm inspects a tubular size or applies a normative document that is not in the annexed scope, so the report cannot legitimately carry the accreditation mark

facets.q: Does ONAC require a separate procedure for PAUT?

facets.q: What is the most common PAUT finding at audit?

facets.q: Does ONAC require a separate procedure for ET?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a ET procedure under ONAC?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in ET. Because ONAC accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover ET, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What ET records does a ONAC audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's ET certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, and the reference standards carrying the notches or holes used to set the response. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common ET finding at audit?
facets.a: Reference standard not representative of the material or geometry examined. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under ONAC is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform ET under ONAC?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does ET need under ONAC?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do ET requirements differ from the other methods in ONAC?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. ONAC also covers UT including B-scan thickness measurement, MFL (magnetic flux leakage), PAUT, RT, MT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for ET
paragraphs: Colombia is the regional exception: it has a domestic third-party route. ONAC accredits certification bodies for persons under ISO/IEC 17024, and ACOSEND has held that accreditation to certify NDT inspectors at Levels I and II against ISO 9712:2012 in MT, PT, RT, UT and VT; verify current status in ONAC's Directorio Oficial de Acreditados before relying on it. Level III is not covered domestically, so Level III comes from ASNT or a foreign ISO 9712 body. Employer certification under SNT-TC-1A remains common in operator supply chains, but inside an ONAC-accredited inspection body personnel competence must be demonstrated against ISO/IEC 17020 clause 6.1, not merely against the employer's written practice.

facets.q: Who does SAE (ex-OAE) apply to?
facets.a: NDT and inspection contractors working Ecuadorian oil and gas: the Oriente basin fields, the SOTE and OCP pipelines, the Esmeraldas and Shushufindi refineries and the fuel terminals, plus tank farms, power plants and metalwork fabrication. It binds any firm that must present itself as an accredited inspection body, or be qualified by ARCH to inspect for an operator.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for SAE (ex-OAE) compliance?
facets.a: Yes. SAE (ex-OAE) accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a SAE (ex-OAE) audit ask for?
facets.a: Solicitud de acreditación filed through SISAC with all annexes, plus payment of the file-opening fee, Management system documentation against NTE INEN-ISO/IEC 17020:2013, including the type A, B or C declaration and the impartiality analysis, Alcance de acreditación drafted in SAE's format, naming each inspection activity and the normative documents it is performed and judged against, Práctica escrita and personnel certification files by method and level, with authorisation records and ongoing competence monitoring evidence, NDT procedures approved by the Level III and traceable to the codes the client cites, typically ASME, API and AWS. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is SAE (ex-OAE) renewed?
facets.a: SAE accreditation runs for five years and is maintained by two surveillance evaluations at eighteen-month intervals within the cycle; reaccreditation must be applied for before the cycle expires. Scope extension is available at any point on demonstration of conformity, and accreditation can be withdrawn where non-compliance affects technical competence or the quality of results. ARCH qualification runs on its own cycle set by the agency and must be tracked as a separate diary item; firms routinely lose work by keeping one current and letting the other lapse. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common SAE (ex-OAE) findings?
facets.a: Documents, contracts and certificates still cite "OAE", so the entity named does not match SAE's current register and the client's procurement system rejects it, The witnessing stage fails because the inspector observed on site is not the one whose competence file was submitted, Scope written in generic terms such as "ensayos no destructivos" rather than by activity and normative document, so SAE cannot grant it as drafted, Surveillance evaluation missed because the firm tracked the five-year expiry but not the eighteen-month surveillance points inside the cycle. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does SAE (ex-OAE) cover?
facets.a: UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, Thickness measurement. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under SAE (ex-OAE)
paragraphs: Employer-based certification is accepted and is the norm. Ecuador has no verified accredited domestic body certifying NDT personnel to ISO 9712, so technicians hold employer certification written against ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or ISO 9712 certificates issued abroad. An outsourced Level III can sign the written practice, approve NDT procedures and certify Level I and II staff. The constraint sits on the other side of the transaction: inside a SAE-accredited inspection body, personnel competence must be demonstrated to the assessor against NTE INEN-ISO/IEC 17020:2013, meaning training, formal authorisation, witnessed performance and ongoing monitoring records. An SNT-TC-1A card on its own is not sufficient evidence at a SAE witnessing evaluation.

facets.q: How long does SAE (ex-OAE) audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Servicio de Acreditación Ecuatoriano (SAE) as the national accreditation body; Agencia de Regulación y Control de Hidrocarburos (ARCH), re-established by Decreto Ejecutivo 256 of 8 May 2024 under the Ministerio de Energía y Minas, for hydrocarbon-sector qualification of inspection companies look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common SAE (ex-OAE) findings?
facets.a: Documents, contracts and certificates still cite "OAE", so the entity named does not match SAE's current register and the client's procurement system rejects it, The witnessing stage fails because the inspector observed on site is not the one whose competence file was submitted, Scope written in generic terms such as "ensayos no destructivos" rather than by activity and normative document, so SAE cannot grant it as drafted, Surveillance evaluation missed because the firm tracked the five-year expiry but not the eighteen-month surveillance points inside the cycle. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the SAE (ex-OAE) audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a SAE (ex-OAE) finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does SAE (ex-OAE) require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first SAE (ex-OAE) audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: Does SAE (ex-OAE) require a separate procedure for UT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a UT procedure under SAE (ex-OAE)?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in UT. Because SAE (ex-OAE) accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover UT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What UT records does a SAE (ex-OAE) audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's UT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, cables, couplant, and the calibration and reference blocks used to set sensitivity. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common UT finding at audit?
facets.a: An in-calibration instrument used with an unidentified or out-of-calibration reference block. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under SAE (ex-OAE) is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform UT under SAE (ex-OAE)?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does UT need under SAE (ex-OAE)?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do UT requirements differ from the other methods in SAE (ex-OAE)?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. SAE (ex-OAE) also covers PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

Accreditation is granted for five years, maintained by two surveillance evaluations at eighteen-month intervals inside the cycle, with reaccreditation applied for before expiry. In the hydrocarbon sector operators additionally require ARCH qualification, so accreditation alone does not open the gate.

SAE accreditation runs for five years and is maintained by two surveillance evaluations at eighteen-month intervals within the cycle; reaccreditation must be applied for before the cycle expires. Scope extension is available at any point on demonstration of conformity, and accreditation can be withdrawn where non-compliance affects technical competence or the quality of results. ARCH qualification runs on its own cycle set by the agency and must be tracked as a separate diary item; firms routinely lose work by keeping one current and letting the other lapse.
Applies to the personnel certification behind this method

facets.q: Does SAE (ex-OAE) require a separate procedure for ET?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a ET procedure under SAE (ex-OAE)?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in ET. Because SAE (ex-OAE) accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover ET, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What ET records does a SAE (ex-OAE) audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's ET certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, and the reference standards carrying the notches or holes used to set the response. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common ET finding at audit?
facets.a: Reference standard not representative of the material or geometry examined. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under SAE (ex-OAE) is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform ET under SAE (ex-OAE)?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does ET need under SAE (ex-OAE)?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do ET requirements differ from the other methods in SAE (ex-OAE)?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. SAE (ex-OAE) also covers UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for ET
paragraphs: Employer-based certification is accepted and is the norm. Ecuador has no verified accredited domestic body certifying NDT personnel to ISO 9712, so technicians hold employer certification written against ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or ISO 9712 certificates issued abroad. An outsourced Level III can sign the written practice, approve NDT procedures and certify Level I and II staff. The constraint sits on the other side of the transaction: inside a SAE-accredited inspection body, personnel competence must be demonstrated to the assessor against NTE INEN-ISO/IEC 17020:2013, meaning training, formal authorisation, witnessed performance and ongoing monitoring records. An SNT-TC-1A card on its own is not sufficient evidence at a SAE witnessing evaluation.

title: COVENIN / SENCAMER Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: NDT and inspection contractors working the Venezuelan oil, gas and petrochemical estate: Faja del Orinoco upgraders, the Paraguaná, Puerto La Cruz and El Palito.
h1: COVENIN / SENCAMER Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: NDT and inspection contractors working the Venezuelan oil, gas and petrochemical estate: Faja del Orinoco upgraders, the Paraguaná, Puerto La Cruz and El Palito refineries, gas processing plant and the PDVSA pipeline network, plus steel and aluminium at Ciudad Guayana, power generation and shipyards. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: It binds any firm certifying NDT personnel or claiming accredited status inside Venezuela. COVENIN is the designation carried by the Venezuelan national standard, not a live commission. The Comisión Venezolana de Normas Industriales was created in 1958, and authority to issue COVENIN standards now sits with SENCAMER. For an NDT service provider the operative document is COVENIN 1999:2021, the third revision of the requirements for qualification and certification of NDT personnel, which completely replaces COVENIN 1999:1999 and was revised by technical committee CT22 Ensayos No Destructivos under SENCAMER's guidelines, aligning Venezuelan requirements with ISO 9712. COVENIN 2967:2021 covers NDT training and qualification centres. SENCAMER also administers the NORVEN conformity mark and the accreditation of conformity assessment bodies, including inspection bodies and testing laboratories.

facets.q: Who does COVENIN / SENCAMER apply to?
facets.a: NDT and inspection contractors working the Venezuelan oil, gas and petrochemical estate: Faja del Orinoco upgraders, the Paraguaná, Puerto La Cruz and El Palito refineries, gas processing plant and the PDVSA pipeline network, plus steel and aluminium at Ciudad Guayana, power generation and shipyards. It binds any firm certifying NDT personnel or claiming accredited status inside Venezuela.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for COVENIN / SENCAMER compliance?
facets.a: Yes. COVENIN / SENCAMER accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a COVENIN / SENCAMER audit ask for?
facets.a: Certificados de calificación y certificación per COVENIN 1999:2021, by method and level, where the contract calls up the national scheme, Práctica escrita to ASNT SNT-TC-1A signed by the Level III, with education, training, experience and examination requirements per method, where the contract runs on the employer model, Training records from a centre meeting COVENIN 2967:2021 requirements, supporting the training hours claimed, Written NDT procedures approved by the Level III and traceable to the code the client cites: ASME BPVC Section V, API 1104, AWS D1.1 or the applicable PDVSA specification, Vision examination records covering near vision and colour differentiation, dated within the last twelve months. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is COVENIN / SENCAMER renewed?
facets.a: COVENIN 1999:2021 aligns Venezuelan personnel certification with ISO 9712, whose cycle is five years with a single renewal and recertification at ten years; treat that as the working assumption but confirm it against the text of COVENIN 1999:2021 itself, which could not be read directly from SENCAMER's catalogue server. Where the contract runs on employer certification instead, the interval is whatever the written practice states, commonly five years for Levels I and II with annual vision checks. SENCAMER accreditation cycle lengths are not published on its public pages, so do not quote one. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common COVENIN / SENCAMER findings?
facets.a: Certificates issued against COVENIN 1999:1999, which COVENIN 1999:2021 completely replaced, still in circulation and being treated as current, The written practice recites SNT-TC-1A but sets shorter training or experience hours than the recommended practice, with no documented technical justification, Training hours claimed from a centre that does not meet COVENIN 2967:2021 requirements for NDT training and qualification centres, Vision records missing, or older than twelve months, for technicians on active assignment. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does COVENIN / SENCAMER cover?
facets.a: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, AE (acoustic emission), Thickness measurement. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under COVENIN / SENCAMER
paragraphs: Mixed, and the mix is commercially decisive. COVENIN 1999:2021 sets out a national qualification and certification scheme aligned with ISO 9712, which is a central rather than employer model, and COVENIN 2967:2021 governs the training and qualification centres that feed it. But a functioning SENCAMER-accredited ISO/IEC 17024 body certifying NDT personnel could not be verified, and in practice the PDVSA supply chain has long run on employer certification written against ASNT SNT-TC-1A, with ISO 9712 certificates from foreign bodies for staff who also work internationally. An outsourced Level III can sign the written practice; whether the client accepts that in place of COVENIN 1999 certification is a contract question, so settle it in the tender documents before mobilising.

facets.q: How long does COVENIN / SENCAMER audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does SENCAMER, the national standardisation, quality, metrology and technical regulation service, which is the current issuer of COVENIN standards and operates the accreditation subsystem under the Ley Orgánica del Sistema Venezolano para la Calidad look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common COVENIN / SENCAMER findings?
facets.a: Certificates issued against COVENIN 1999:1999, which COVENIN 1999:2021 completely replaced, still in circulation and being treated as current, The written practice recites SNT-TC-1A but sets shorter training or experience hours than the recommended practice, with no documented technical justification, Training hours claimed from a centre that does not meet COVENIN 2967:2021 requirements for NDT training and qualification centres, Vision records missing, or older than twelve months, for technicians on active assignment. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the COVENIN / SENCAMER audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a COVENIN / SENCAMER finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does COVENIN / SENCAMER require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first COVENIN / SENCAMER audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.
