facets.q: Does COVENIN / SENCAMER require a separate procedure for UT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a UT procedure under COVENIN / SENCAMER?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in UT. Because COVENIN / SENCAMER accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover UT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What UT records does a COVENIN / SENCAMER audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's UT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, cables, couplant, and the calibration and reference blocks used to set sensitivity. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common UT finding at audit?
facets.a: An in-calibration instrument used with an unidentified or out-of-calibration reference block. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under COVENIN / SENCAMER is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform UT under COVENIN / SENCAMER?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does UT need under COVENIN / SENCAMER?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do UT requirements differ from the other methods in COVENIN / SENCAMER?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. COVENIN / SENCAMER also covers RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

facets.q: What is the most common RT finding at audit?

title: TTBS / OSH Act Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: NDT and inspection contractors serving the Point Lisas ammonia, methanol and iron estate, Atlantic LNG at Point Fortin, the Pointe-à-Pierre refinery complex, Heritag
h1: TTBS / OSH Act Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: NDT and inspection contractors serving the Point Lisas ammonia, methanol and iron estate, Atlantic LNG at Point Fortin, the Pointe-à-Pierre refinery complex, Heritage and Touchstone upstream, offshore platforms and the marine and dry-dock trade. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: It binds any firm examining steam boilers or air pressure containers, and any firm claiming accredited inspection status locally. Trinidad and Tobago has no NDT-specific regime, and the gap itself is the commercially important fact. TTBS's accreditation arm, TTLABS, accredits laboratories to ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO 15189 only, so there is no domestic route to ISO/IEC 17020 inspection body accreditation; firms go to JANAAC in Jamaica or to a foreign accreditation body, which is how TTBS's own Implementation Division came to hold ISO/IEC 17020:2012 accreditation. What is legally binding sits elsewhere. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, Chap. 88:08, and the Boilers Regulations and Air Pressure Containers Regulations continued in force by section 98(2), steam boilers and air pressure containers must be thoroughly examined every twelve months by a person holding a Ministerial licence who is independent of the occupier, owner or hirer.
source: Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2004 (Act No. 1 of 2004), Chap. 88:08, as amended by Act No. 3 of 2006, Laws of Trinidad and Tobago revised edition, read directly: the Occupational Safety and Health (Prescribed Forms) Order (GN 187-1948) items 18 Hoists or Lifts, 19 Steam Boilers and 20 Air Pressure Containers; the Boilers Regulations (GN 2-1949) including the annual and other examinations provisions, the boiler examiner licence and independence requirement, Gazette publication of licences and the list of boiler examiners on 1 January each year, and the twenty-one day report filing period; the Special Provisions for Safety in the Case of Air Pressure Containers Regulations (GN 3-1949) including the competent person requirement; all continued in force by section 98(2). The Act, except section 98, came into operation by Proclamation LN 48/2006 on 17 February 2006, with section 98 brought into force by 17 August 2007, repealing the Factories Ordinance (Ch. 30 No. 2), the Employment of Women (Night Work) Act and the Gas Cylinders (Use, Conveyance and Storage) Act. TTBS website and TTLABS accreditation page (accessed August 2026) confirming accreditation to ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO 15189, ILAC and IAAC membership, and that the TTBS Implementation Division operates as an ISO/IEC 17020:2012 inspection body accredited by JANAAC; JANAAC website confirming ISO/IEC 17020 among its scopes alongside ISO/IEC 17025, ISO/IEC 17021-1 and ISO 15189, and its IAAC MLA and ILAC MRA signatory status; CROSQ report of TTBS Certification Division accreditation by JANAAC to ISO/IEC 17021-1:2015 on 3 October 2022. facets.q: Who does TTBS / OSH Act apply to?
facets.a: NDT and inspection contractors serving the Point Lisas ammonia, methanol and iron estate, Atlantic LNG at Point Fortin, the Pointe-à-Pierre refinery complex, Heritage and Touchstone upstream, offshore platforms and the marine and dry-dock trade. It binds any firm examining steam boilers or air pressure containers, and any firm claiming accredited inspection status locally.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for TTBS / OSH Act compliance?
facets.a: Yes. TTBS / OSH Act accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a TTBS / OSH Act audit ask for?
facets.a: Written practice to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, signed and dated by the Level III, covering every method, level and technique the company offers, Personnel certification files with training records, documented experience, examination papers and grading, and current near-vision and colour differentiation records, Written NDT procedures approved by the Level III against the code the client cites: ASME BPVC Section V, API 510, API 570, API 653 or AWS D1.1, Boiler examiner's licence issued by the Minister, unsuspended and uncancelled, for anyone examining steam boilers, economisers, superheaters or air pressure containers, Prescribed Form No. 7, report of examination of the boiler when cold, signed by the person making the examination. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is TTBS / OSH Act renewed?
facets.a: The statutory intervals are fixed and verifiable. Steam boilers and all fittings and attachments: thorough examination at least once in every period of twelve months and also after any extensive repairs, with the twelve months running from completion of the examination under normal steam pressure; the competent person may extend that period by not more than one month in an emergency where shutdown would cause serious loss or damage, after which the next examination must fall within the succeeding eleven months. Air pressure containers: thoroughly cleaned, examined and hydraulically tested every twelve months. Hoists and lifts: thoroughly examined every twelve months. Boiler examiners' licences and the examination fee schedule are published in the Gazette on 1 January each year. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common TTBS / OSH Act findings?
facets.a: Boiler examination performed by an NDT contractor's Level II or Level III holding no Ministerial boiler examiner's licence, The examiner is on the occupier's payroll, or the owner's or hirer's, breaching the independence requirement the Boilers Regulations impose, Only the cold examination performed and the examination under normal steam pressure omitted, so the twelve-month clock never legitimately restarts, Forms 7 and 8 completed but not entered in or attached to the General Register within twenty-one days of the examination. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does TTBS / OSH Act cover?
facets.a: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under TTBS / OSH Act
paragraphs: Employer-based certification is accepted for NDT, and is dominant. There is no local ISO 9712 certification body, and TTLABS does not accredit personnel certification bodies, so technicians hold employer certification written against ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the norm across the US-influenced petrochemical estate, or PCN and other ISO 9712 certificates issued in the UK. An outsourced Level III can write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and certify Level I and II staff. The statutory boiler and pressure-vessel examination is a separate and stricter matter: it requires a licence from the Minister plus personal independence from the equipment's owner, and no NDT certification substitutes for it.

sections.heading: The audit sequence
items: Establish the statutory route first: identify which items on the client's site are steam boilers, economisers, superheaters or air pressure containers under the Act, because those require a Ministerially licensed examiner, not merely a certified NDT technician
Confirm the examiner's licence is current and that he is not in the employ of the occupier of the premises, nor of the owner or hirer of the equipment
Carry out the examination in the prescribed order: the boiler cold, with interior and exterior prepared to the examiner's satisfaction, then under normal steam pressure
Report on Forms 7 and 8, signed by the person making the examination, and enter or attach them to the General Register within twenty-one days
Where the client requires third-party accreditation, apply to JANAAC or another recognised accreditation body for ISO/IEC 17020 accreditation, since TTLABS does not offer that scheme
Maintain the twelve-month cycle, dated from completion of the examination under normal steam pressure

Personnel certification files with training records, documented experience, examination papers and grading, and current near-vision and colour differentiation records
Written NDT procedures approved by the Level III against the code the client cites: ASME BPVC Section V, API 510, API 570, API 653 or AWS D1.1

h1: TTBS / OSH Act Audit Preparation for Inspection Companies
answer: A TTBS / OSH Act audit runs in 6 stages, beginning with establish the statutory route first: identify which items on the client's site.. Trinidad and Tobago Bureau of Standards (TTBS), including its laboratory accreditation arm TTLABS; the Occupational Safety and Health Authority and Agency; the Minister responsible, who licenses boiler examiners; the Ministry of Energy and Energy Industries for petroleum operations tests the system by sampling finished.
expansion: Trinidad and Tobago has no NDT-specific regime, and the gap itself is the commercially important fact. facets.q: How long does TTBS / OSH Act audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Trinidad and Tobago Bureau of Standards (TTBS), including its laboratory accreditation arm TTLABS; the Occupational Safety and Health Authority and Agency; the Minister responsible, who licenses boiler examiners; the Ministry of Energy and Energy Industries for petroleum operations look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common TTBS / OSH Act findings?
facets.a: Boiler examination performed by an NDT contractor's Level II or Level III holding no Ministerial boiler examiner's licence, The examiner is on the occupier's payroll, or the owner's or hirer's, breaching the independence requirement the Boilers Regulations impose, Only the cold examination performed and the examination under normal steam pressure omitted, so the twelve-month clock never legitimately restarts, Forms 7 and 8 completed but not entered in or attached to the General Register within twenty-one days of the examination. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the TTBS / OSH Act audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a TTBS / OSH Act finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does TTBS / OSH Act require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first TTBS / OSH Act audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: What must a written practice contain under TTBS / OSH Act?
facets.a: It has to satisfy TTBS / OSH Act as Trinidad and Tobago Bureau of Standards (TTBS), including its laboratory accreditation arm TTLABS; the Occupational Safety and Health Authority and Agency; the Minister responsible, who licenses boiler examiners; the Ministry of Energy and Energy Industries for petroleum operations enforces it: the document that defines how the employer qualifies and certifies its own NDT personnel. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the written practice for TTBS / OSH Act?
facets.a: The employer's Level III. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a TTBS / OSH Act auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must TTBS / OSH Act records be kept?
facets.a: The statutory intervals are fixed and verifiable. Steam boilers and all fittings and attachments: thorough examination at least once in every period of twelve months and also after any extensive repairs, with the twelve months running from completion of the examination under normal steam pressure; the competent person may extend that period by not more than one month in an emergency where shutdown would cause serious loss or damage, after which the next examination must fall within the succeeding eleven months. Air pressure containers: thoroughly cleaned, examined and hydraulically tested every twelve months. Hoists and lifts: thoroughly examined every twelve months. Boiler examiners' licences and the examination fee schedule are published in the Gazette on 1 January each year. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy TTBS / OSH Act?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a TTBS / OSH Act audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: Boiler examination performed by an NDT contractor's Level II or Level III holding no Ministerial boiler examiner's licence

title: PAUT Requirements Under TTBS / OSH Act
description: What TTBS / OSH Act requires for Phased Array Ultrasonics: procedure approval, personnel qualification, equipment evidence and what an auditor samples.
h1: Phased Array Ultrasonics (PAUT) Requirements Under TTBS / OSH Act
answer: Procedure qualification usually requires a demonstration on a representative flawed sample, and the scan plan forms part of the approved procedure rather than a field decision. TTBS / OSH Act, enforced by Trinidad and Tobago Bureau of Standards (TTBS), including its laboratory accreditation arm.: Employer-based certification is accepted for NDT, and is dominant.
expansion: An auditor examining PAUT asks for the phased array unit, wedges, encoders, and the calibration blocks used for wedge delay, sensitivity and TCG. Trinidad and Tobago has no NDT-specific regime, and the gap itself is the commercially important fact. TTBS's accreditation arm, TTLABS, accredits laboratories to ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO 15189 only, so there is no domestic route to ISO/IEC 17020 inspection body accreditation; firms go to JANAAC in Jamaica or to a foreign accreditation body, which is how TTBS's own Implementation Division came to hold ISO/IEC 17020:2012 accreditation. What is legally binding sits elsewhere. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, Chap. 88:08, and the Boilers Regulations and Air Pressure Containers Regulations continued in force by section 98(2), steam boilers and air pressure containers must be thoroughly examined every twelve months by a person holding a Ministerial licence who is independent of the occupier, owner or hirer.
source: Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2004 (Act No. 1 of 2004), Chap. 88:08, as amended by Act No. 3 of 2006, Laws of Trinidad and Tobago revised edition, read directly: the Occupational Safety and Health (Prescribed Forms) Order (GN 187-1948) items 18 Hoists or Lifts, 19 Steam Boilers and 20 Air Pressure Containers; the Boilers Regulations (GN 2-1949) including the annual and other examinations provisions, the boiler examiner licence and independence requirement, Gazette publication of licences and the list of boiler examiners on 1 January each year, and the twenty-one day report filing period; the Special Provisions for Safety in the Case of Air Pressure Containers Regulations (GN 3-1949) including the competent person requirement; all continued in force by section 98(2). The Act, except section 98, came into operation by Proclamation LN 48/2006 on 17 February 2006, with section 98 brought into force by 17 August 2007, repealing the Factories Ordinance (Ch. 30 No. 2), the Employment of Women (Night Work) Act and the Gas Cylinders (Use, Conveyance and Storage) Act. TTBS website and TTLABS accreditation page (accessed August 2026) confirming accreditation to ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO 15189, ILAC and IAAC membership, and that the TTBS Implementation Division operates as an ISO/IEC 17020:2012 inspection body accredited by JANAAC; JANAAC website confirming ISO/IEC 17020 among its scopes alongside ISO/IEC 17025, ISO/IEC 17021-1 and ISO 15189, and its IAAC MLA and ILAC MRA signatory status; CROSQ report of TTBS Certification Division accreditation by JANAAC to ISO/IEC 17021-1:2015 on 3 October 2022. The Standards Act number and chapter establishing TTBS could not be verified from a primary source in this session and is therefore not stated.

title: Nadcap NDT / AC7114 Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Any site that performs NDT on aerospace hardware: independent inspection service providers and NDT test houses, and captive NDT departments inside machining, casting
h1: Nadcap NDT / AC7114 Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Any site that performs NDT on aerospace hardware: independent inspection service providers and NDT test houses, and captive NDT departments inside machining, casting, forging, fabrication and MRO shops. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: It binds when a subscribing prime — Boeing, GE Aviation, Pratt & Whitney, Rolls-Royce, Collins Aerospace, Safran, Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, Sikorsky, Bell, Eaton — flows Nadcap accreditation down as a purchase-order condition. Accreditation is granted per site and per method, not per company. AC7114 is the base checklist of the Nadcap NDT programme, and it audits the NDT quality system rather than any one method. It covers customer requirement flowdown and the sequencing of NDT operations, procurement control over sub-tier calibration and cleaning/etching facilities, an annual internal NDT audit, control and traceability of inspection status identifiers, inspection and traveller records, and calibration including interval extension. Section 5 audits people: the written practice, certification packages, vision records, the Responsible Level 3, outside Level 3 agencies and training course outlines. AC7114 is never used alone — every accredited method adds a slash sheet, and each prime may add a supplemental question set. The general quality system is covered by AS9100/EN9100, AC7004, or ISO/IEC 17025 for test houses.
source: AC7114 Rev L (Issued 1997-07, Revised 21-SEP-2017, superseding Rev K, to be used on audits starting on or after 31-DEC-2017) read in full for question numbering and Compliance Assessment Guidance. facets.q: Who does Nadcap NDT / AC7114 apply to?
facets.a: Any site that performs NDT on aerospace hardware: independent inspection service providers and NDT test houses, and captive NDT departments inside machining, casting, forging, fabrication and MRO shops. It binds when a subscribing prime — Boeing, GE Aviation, Pratt & Whitney, Rolls-Royce, Collins Aerospace, Safran, Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, Sikorsky, Bell, Eaton — flows Nadcap accreditation down as a purchase-order condition. Accreditation is granted per site and per method, not per company.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for Nadcap NDT / AC7114 compliance?
facets.a: Yes. Nadcap NDT / AC7114 accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a Nadcap NDT / AC7114 audit ask for?
facets.a: Completed self-audit checklists — AC7114 plus every applicable slash sheet and supplement — uploaded to eAuditNet no less than 30 days before the scheduled audit, with the procedure and paragraph referenced for each question, NDT written practice for qualification and certification of personnel, approved by the Responsible Level 3, NDT method process procedures, plus the work instructions known in industry as technique sheets or data cards, List of Approved NDT Personnel including Level 3's, on attachment AC7114-A, NDT material and equipment list for each method on attachments AC7114/1A through AC7114/9A. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is Nadcap NDT / AC7114 renewed?
facets.a: Initial accreditation is 12 months. PRI states it can be extended to 18 months based on audit performance after three audits, and to 24 months after five audits, under the Supplier Merit Program. Both lengths appear on real certificates: an 18-month accreditation expiring 31 May 2023 and a 24-month accreditation expiring 31 May 2026 and 28 February 2027. facets.q: How long does Nadcap NDT / AC7114 audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Performance Review Institute (PRI), a not-for-profit affiliate of SAE International, administering Nadcap on behalf of the Nadcap NDT Task Group and its subscribing primes look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common Nadcap NDT / AC7114 findings?
facets.a: Self-audit uploaded late, performed against a superseded checklist revision, or not including one compliance job per method (AC7114 question 4), Written practice not approved by the Responsible Level 3, or failing to identify every method and specific technique actually performed at the site, Techniques shown on an individual's certificate that do not appear as techniques in the written practice (question 5.2.3), Near-vision examination not repeated annually, colour perception not repeated at least every five years, or the exam administered by someone not designated in writing by the Responsible Level 3 (questions 5.4.6, 5.4.7). Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the Nadcap NDT / AC7114 audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a Nadcap NDT / AC7114 finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does Nadcap NDT / AC7114 require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first Nadcap NDT / AC7114 audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: How does a Nadcap NDT / AC7114 auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must Nadcap NDT / AC7114 records be kept?

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy Nadcap NDT / AC7114?

facets.q: Does Nadcap NDT / AC7114 require a separate procedure for PT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a PT procedure under Nadcap NDT / AC7114?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in PT. Because Nadcap NDT / AC7114 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover PT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What PT records does a Nadcap NDT / AC7114 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's PT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — penetrant, developer, cleaner and emulsifier batch records, plus the light meters for the inspection environment. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common PT finding at audit?
facets.a: Batch certificates missing for consumables used, or dwell time not recorded. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under Nadcap NDT / AC7114 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform PT under Nadcap NDT / AC7114?

answer: Every Nadcap NDT auditee, because the base AC7114 alone cannot be accredited. sections.heading: Personnel certification under AC7114 slash sheets

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the AC7114 slash sheets audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a AC7114 slash sheets finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does AC7114 slash sheets require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first AC7114 slash sheets audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: What must a equipment calibration records contain under AC7114 slash sheets?
facets.a: It has to satisfy AC7114 slash sheets as Performance Review Institute (PRI) — Nadcap NDT Task Group; the supplemental 'S' sheets are owned by the individual subscribing primes enforces it: the traceable evidence that every instrument was in calibration on the day it was used. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the equipment calibration records for AC7114 slash sheets?
facets.a: The equipment custodian. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a AC7114 slash sheets auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must AC7114 slash sheets records be kept?
facets.a: The slash sheets follow the base accreditation cycle — 12 months initially, extendable to 18 and then 24 months under the Supplier Merit Program — but each document is revised on its own clock. A single 2025-dated certificate shows AC7114 Rev S effective for audits on/after 19-May-2024, AC7114/2 Rev P and AC7114/3 Rev O both on/after 17-Mar-2024, and AC7114/1 Rev O marked for audits before 16-Feb-2025, meaning a newer revision took effect mid-cycle. Revision effectivity must be re-checked before every audit, not once per accreditation. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy AC7114 slash sheets?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a AC7114 slash sheets audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: Scope on the Qualified Manufacturers List does not match what the shop runs — most often digital radiography or computed radiography performed while only the film radiography sheet AC7114/4 is on the scope

title: FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: NDT firms whose inspection results are used to return civil aeronautical articles to service.
h1: FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: NDT firms whose inspection results are used to return civil aeronautical articles to service. A standalone NDT house needs its own repair station certificate carrying the §145.61(b)(9) limited rating for nondestructive inspection, testing, and processing. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: Alternatively the firm works as a noncertificated contractor to a repair station, in which case the repair station must qualify and surveil it under its own quality control system. Covers aircraft, engines, propellers, accessories and components. Part 145 does not describe NDT techniques; it regulates the organisation that performs them. The FAA issues a limited rating for 'Nondestructive inspection, testing, and processing' under §145.61(b)(9), and §145.61(c) requires the repair station's operations specifications to name the specification used for the specialized service — either a civil or military specification currently used by industry and approved by the FAA, or one the applicant develops and the FAA approves. Around that sit §145.151 personnel, §145.155 inspection personnel proficiency and English literacy, §145.163 an FAA-approved initial and recurrent training program with records kept at least two years, and §145.211(c) a quality control manual that must describe how inspection personnel proficiency is established and maintained and how measuring and test equipment is calibrated, including intervals.
source: 14 CFR §§145.51, 145.55, 145.59, 145.61, 145.151, 145.155, 145.163, 145.211 as published in the electronic CFR via Cornell LII, current text including Docket FAA-2016-8744 Amdt. 145-31 (81 FR 49163, 27 July 2016) for §145.61 and Amdt. 145-32 (83 FR 9176, 5 March 2018) for §145.163. FAA Advisory Circular 65-31B, 'Training, Qualification, and Certification of Nondestructive Inspection Personnel,' dated 2/24/14, initiated by AFS-300, cancelling AC 65-31A of 25 April 2003, read in full — paragraphs 3, 5d, 5u, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12. Accessed 21 Aug 2026.

Under §145.55(a) a certificate or rating issued to a repair station located in the United States is effective from the date of issue until surrendered and accepted for cancellation, or suspended or revoked — there is no periodic expiry. Under §145.55(b) a certificate issued to a repair station located outside the United States expires on the last day of the 12th month after issue and the FAA may renew it for 24 months; renewal must be requested no later than 30 days before expiry and the prescribed fee paid, otherwise the full §145.51 application procedure applies. facets.q: Who does FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) apply to?
facets.a: NDT firms whose inspection results are used to return civil aeronautical articles to service. A standalone NDT house needs its own repair station certificate carrying the §145.61(b)(9) limited rating for nondestructive inspection, testing, and processing. Alternatively the firm works as a noncertificated contractor to a repair station, in which case the repair station must qualify and surveil it under its own quality control system. Covers aircraft, engines, propellers, accessories and components.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) compliance?
facets.a: Yes. FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) audit ask for?
facets.a: Application for a repair station certificate and rating, with the attachments required by §145.51(a), Operations specifications containing the specification used to perform the specialized service, per §145.61(c), Repair station manual, and the quality control manual required by §145.211(c) covering preliminary, hidden-damage and final inspection, establishing and maintaining proficiency of inspection personnel, current technical data, qualifying and surveilling noncertificated persons who perform maintenance, calibration of measuring and test equipment including intervals, and corrective action on deficiencies, FAA-approved employee training program under §145.163(a), submitted per §145.51(a)(7), with individual training records documented and retained a minimum of two years, Written NDI qualification and certification program — the written practice — describing training, examination, qualification, documentation, proficiency maintenance, and the steps to decertify, retrain or recertify (AC 65-31B paragraph 9a). Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) renewed?
facets.a: Under §145.55(a) a certificate or rating issued to a repair station located in the United States is effective from the date of issue until surrendered and accepted for cancellation, or suspended or revoked — there is no periodic expiry. Under §145.55(b) a certificate issued to a repair station located outside the United States expires on the last day of the 12th month after issue and the FAA may renew it for 24 months; renewal must be requested no later than 30 days before expiry and the prescribed fee paid, otherwise the full §145.51 application procedure applies. Personnel recertification runs on the AC 65-31B intervals: Level I Special not exceeding one year, Levels I and II not exceeding three years, Level III at five-year intervals, with requalification also triggered by six months of inactivity in the method or an expired vision examination. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) findings?
facets.a: The specification named in the operations specifications for the NDI specialized service does not match the specification the technicians actually work to, Quality control manual silent on how proficiency of inspection personnel is established and maintained, which §145.211(c)(1)(iv) requires explicitly, Employee training program treated as generic safety training with no method-specific initial and recurrent NDI content, or training records not retained for the full two years required by §145.163(c), Vision examinations lapsed beyond the one-year period, or colour-perception limitations never evaluated and approved in writing by the responsible Level III. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) cover?
facets.a: PT, MT, UT, RT, ET, VT, Eddy current array and phased array where covered by the approved specification and the written practice. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating)
paragraphs: Employer-based, and the FAA says so plainly. AC 65-31B defines certification as 'written testimony of qualification that the employer typically issues' and states: 'In the United States, there is no national certifying agency; therefore, most certifications are employer-based and are not transferrable.' The AC lists acceptable standards — AIA-NAS-410, ATA Specification 105, CAN/CGSB-48.9712-95, ISO 9712, MIL-STD-410E (rescinded but acceptable), ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and prEN 4179. It defines an 'Outside Agency' as an independent body under contract for NDI services, explicitly including consultants and self-employed individuals, and paragraph 9b permits a qualified outside agency to provide NDI training, qualification and testing at the organisation's option and as provided in its written practice.

sections.heading: The audit sequence
items: Pre-application discussion with the responsible Flight Standards office to agree the rating sought and the specification that will be named in the operations specifications for the NDI specialized service.
Formal application under §145.51 with the repair station manual, quality control manual and the employee training program required by §145.51(a)(7).
FAA review of the submitted manuals and program for compliance with §§145.207, 145.209, 145.211 and 145.163, with revision cycles until they are acceptable to the FAA.

On-site evaluation of housing, facilities, equipment, materials and data under §145.109, and demonstration that inspection personnel meet §145.155 and that the quality control system is actually being followed.
Issue of the certificate, the ratings and limitations, and the operations specifications naming the approved NDI specification.

Continued operational surveillance by the responsible Flight Standards office, with revisions to the quality control manual notified under §145.211(d) and training program revisions submitted under §145.163(d).

sections.heading: Documents an auditor asks for
items: Application for a repair station certificate and rating, with the attachments required by §145.51(a)
Operations specifications containing the specification used to perform the specialized service, per §145.61(c)

Repair station manual, and the quality control manual required by §145.211(c) covering preliminary, hidden-damage and final inspection, establishing and maintaining proficiency of inspection personnel, current technical data, qualifying and surveilling noncertificated persons who perform maintenance, calibration of measuring and test equipment including intervals, and corrective action on deficiencies
FAA-approved employee training program under §145.163(a), submitted per §145.51(a)(7), with individual training records documented and retained a minimum of two years

Written NDI qualification and certification program — the written practice — describing training, examination, qualification, documentation, proficiency maintenance, and the steps to decertify, retrain or recertify (AC 65-31B paragraph 9a)

Personnel records specifying date, time and place of qualification, employing organisation, level, special qualifications or limitations, and the standard under which the individual is qualified, including a copy of any FAA repairman certificate issued to that individual (AC 65-31B paragraph 12)

Vision examination records — near vision to Snellen 20/25 or Jaeger #1 in at least one eye, corrected or uncorrected, on a periodic basis not exceeding one year; colour perception evaluated once at initial examination with any limitation approved in writing by the responsible Level III
Calibration records for NDI instruments traceable to a national metrological institute such as NIST
Contracting arrangements and evidence of qualification and surveillance for any noncertificated person performing maintenance functions, as required by §145.151(d) and the quality control manual

sections.heading: Findings firms get against FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating)
items: The specification named in the operations specifications for the NDI specialized service does not match the specification the technicians actually work to
Quality control manual silent on how proficiency of inspection personnel is established and maintained, which §145.211(c)(1)(iv) requires explicitly
Employee training program treated as generic safety training with no method-specific initial and recurrent NDI content, or training records not retained for the full two years required by §145.163(c)
Vision examinations lapsed beyond the one-year period, or colour-perception limitations never evaluated and approved in writing by the responsible Level III
Written practice references SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410 but the recertification intervals actually applied do not match the standard the organisation says it follows
Outside agency used for training, qualification or testing without that use being provided for in the written practice, as AC 65-31B paragraph 9b requires

facets.q: How long does FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Federal Aviation Administration, Flight Standards Service; day-to-day oversight sits with the repair station's responsible Flight Standards office look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) findings?
facets.a: The specification named in the operations specifications for the NDI specialized service does not match the specification the technicians actually work to, Quality control manual silent on how proficiency of inspection personnel is established and maintained, which §145.211(c)(1)(iv) requires explicitly, Employee training program treated as generic safety training with no method-specific initial and recurrent NDI content, or training records not retained for the full two years required by §145.163(c), Vision examinations lapsed beyond the one-year period, or colour-perception limitations never evaluated and approved in writing by the responsible Level III. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: What must a written practice contain under FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating)?

The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the written practice for FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating)?
facets.a: The employer's Level III. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) records be kept?
facets.a: Under §145.55(a) a certificate or rating issued to a repair station located in the United States is effective from the date of issue until surrendered and accepted for cancellation, or suspended or revoked — there is no periodic expiry. Under §145.55(b) a certificate issued to a repair station located outside the United States expires on the last day of the 12th month after issue and the FAA may renew it for 24 months; renewal must be requested no later than 30 days before expiry and the prescribed fee paid, otherwise the full §145.51 application procedure applies. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. facets.q: Does FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) require a separate procedure for PT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a PT procedure under FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating)?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in PT. Because FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover PT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What PT records does a FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) audit sample?

The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common PT finding at audit?
facets.a: Batch certificates missing for consumables used, or dwell time not recorded. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform PT under FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating)?

facets.q: Does FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) require a separate procedure for VT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a VT procedure under FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating)?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in VT. Because FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover VT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What VT records does a FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's VT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — light meters, measuring aids, mirrors and borescopes where remote viewing is used. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common VT finding at audit?
facets.a: Illumination at the surface never measured, or near-vision acuity test lapsed. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform VT under FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating)?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does VT need under FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating)?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do VT requirements differ from the other methods in FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating)?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. FAA Part 145 (NDI limited rating) also covers PT, MT, UT, RT, ET, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for VT
paragraphs: Employer-based, and the FAA says so plainly. AC 65-31B defines certification as 'written testimony of qualification that the employer typically issues' and states: 'In the United States, there is no national certifying agency; therefore, most certifications are employer-based and are not transferrable.' The AC lists acceptable standards — AIA-NAS-410, ATA Specification 105, CAN/CGSB-48.9712-95, ISO 9712, MIL-STD-410E (rescinded but acceptable), ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and prEN 4179. It defines an 'Outside Agency' as an independent body under contract for NDI services, explicitly including consultants and self-employed individuals, and paragraph 9b permits a qualified outside agency to provide NDI training, qualification and testing at the organisation's option and as provided in its written practice.

title: 10 CFR 50 Appendix B Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Directly, it binds NRC licensees and applicants.
h1: 10 CFR 50 Appendix B Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Directly, it binds NRC licensees and applicants. Practically it reaches every NDT service provider working on safety-related structures, systems and components, because the licensee flows the criteria down by contract and remains accountable. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: Appendix B states the applicant may delegate the work of establishing and executing the QA program to contractors, agents or consultants but 'shall retain responsibility.' Covers design, manufacture, construction, operation, maintenance, repair, refuelling and modification. Appendix B sets eighteen quality assurance criteria for activities affecting the safety-related functions of nuclear structures, systems and components. For an inspection service provider two criteria bite hardest. Criterion IX, Control of Special Processes, requires measures assuring that special processes 'including welding, heat treating, and nondestructive testing, are controlled and accomplished by qualified personnel using qualified procedures in accordance with applicable codes, standards, specifications, criteria, and other special requirements.' Criterion X, Inspection, requires inspection by individuals other than those who performed the activity being inspected. Criterion XVII requires records identifying the inspector or data recorder, the type of observation, the results, the acceptability and the action taken on any deficiency. Criterion XVIII requires planned periodic audits by trained personnel without direct responsibility in the area audited.

Cross-referenced against 10 CFR Part 21, 'Reporting of Defects and Noncompliance,' same edition, whose definition of 'basic component' at paragraph (4) expressly includes 'safety-related design, analysis, inspection, testing, fabrication, replacement of parts, or consulting services... whether these services are performed by the component supplier or others.' facets.q: Who does 10 CFR 50 Appendix B apply to?
facets.a: Directly, it binds NRC licensees and applicants. Practically it reaches every NDT service provider working on safety-related structures, systems and components, because the licensee flows the criteria down by contract and remains accountable. Appendix B states the applicant may delegate the work of establishing and executing the QA program to contractors, agents or consultants but 'shall retain responsibility.' Covers design, manufacture, construction, operation, maintenance, repair, refuelling and modification.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for 10 CFR 50 Appendix B compliance?
facets.a: Yes. 10 CFR 50 Appendix B accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a 10 CFR 50 Appendix B audit ask for?
facets.a: Quality assurance program description covering all eighteen criteria, with the organisational chart and delegated authorities required by Criterion I, Documented instructions, procedures and drawings for activities affecting quality, with quantitative or qualitative acceptance criteria (Criterion V), Special process procedures for nondestructive testing, with evidence the procedures and the personnel are qualified (Criterion IX), Inspection program showing inspection is performed by individuals other than those who performed the work, and identifying any mandatory hold points (Criterion X), Procurement documents imposing the applicable regulatory, code and QA requirements on sub-tier suppliers (Criterion IV) and the supplier evaluation and assessment records required by Criterion VII. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is 10 CFR 50 Appendix B renewed?
facets.a: Appendix B sets no expiry — it is a standing regulatory requirement, not a certificate. What recurs is verification. Criterion XVIII requires a comprehensive system of planned and periodic audits, and Criterion VII requires the licensee to assess the effectiveness of a supplier's quality control 'at intervals consistent with the importance, complexity, and quantity of the product or services.' For NDT service suppliers this normally lands on the joint utility audit cycle — NUPIC runs most vendors on a 33-month schedule — supplemented by annual internal audits. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common 10 CFR 50 Appendix B findings?
facets.a: QA manual written to the eighteen criteria in the abstract with no procedure translating Criterion IX into control of NDE special processes at the working level, Independence problem under Criterion X — the technician who performed the examination also signs the verifying inspection, Records failing Criterion XVII because the inspection record does not identify the inspector or data recorder, the type of observation, the acceptability, or the action taken on a deficiency, Sub-tier flowdown gaps under Criteria IV and VII — calibration houses, consumables suppliers or contract technicians procured without the applicable QA and 10 CFR Part 21 requirements imposed. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does 10 CFR 50 Appendix B cover?
facets.a: UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, Leak testing. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under 10 CFR 50 Appendix B
paragraphs: Appendix B is method-agnostic and names no certification scheme: Criterion IX simply requires qualified personnel and qualified procedures 'in accordance with applicable codes, standards, specifications.' The scheme therefore comes from whatever code the licensee imposes — in practice ASME Section XI with ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189, or NQA-1. That makes certification employer-based: the supplier writes and owns the written practice and signs the certificates. An outsourced Level III can author and approve the written practice and the NDE procedures and can administer examinations, but Criterion I requires that whoever performs quality assurance verification have organisational freedom and sufficient independence, and the supplier's own management retains the responsibility.

sections.heading: The audit sequence
items: The licensee or its designee evaluates the supplier before award — Criterion VII requires source evaluation and selection, and control of purchased services proportionate to their importance.
The supplier submits its QA program manual and procedures for the licensee's review against the eighteen criteria and against whatever code the contract invokes.

On-site audit by the licensee, its designee, or a joint programme such as NUPIC, performed to written procedures or checklists by trained personnel not having direct responsibilities in the area audited (Criterion XVIII).

Findings are documented and reviewed by management having responsibility in the area audited; the supplier responds with cause determination and corrective action to preclude repetition (Criterion XVI).
Followup, including reaudit of deficient areas where indicated, then placement on the licensee's Approved Suppliers List for the specific scope of services.

Criterion VII requires the effectiveness of the supplier's quality control to be reassessed at intervals consistent with the importance, complexity and quantity of the service — which is what drives the recurring audit cycle.

Internal audit plan, checklists, reports and reaudit records demonstrating a comprehensive system of planned and periodic audits (Criterion XVIII)

facets.q: How long does 10 CFR 50 Appendix B audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common 10 CFR 50 Appendix B findings?
facets.a: QA manual written to the eighteen criteria in the abstract with no procedure translating Criterion IX into control of NDE special processes at the working level, Independence problem under Criterion X — the technician who performed the examination also signs the verifying inspection, Records failing Criterion XVII because the inspection record does not identify the inspector or data recorder, the type of observation, the acceptability, or the action taken on a deficiency, Sub-tier flowdown gaps under Criteria IV and VII — calibration houses, consumables suppliers or contract technicians procured without the applicable QA and 10 CFR Part 21 requirements imposed. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the 10 CFR 50 Appendix B audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a 10 CFR 50 Appendix B finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does 10 CFR 50 Appendix B require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first 10 CFR 50 Appendix B audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

description: What a quality manual ndt section must contain under 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, who signs it, and how U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission tests it at audit.
h1: Quality Manual NDT Section for 10 CFR 50 Appendix B
answer: 10 CFR 50 Appendix B names this requirement as "Quality assurance program description covering all eighteen criteria, with the organisational chart and delegated authorities required by Criterion I". The management representative owns it, and a contracted Level III can author and sign it.
expansion: The finding auditors record against this document is: QA manual written to the eighteen criteria in the abstract with no procedure translating Criterion IX into control of NDE special processes at the working level. Appendix B sets eighteen quality assurance criteria for activities affecting the safety-related functions of nuclear structures, systems and components. For an inspection service provider two criteria bite hardest. Criterion IX, Control of Special Processes, requires measures assuring that special processes 'including welding, heat treating, and nondestructive testing, are controlled and accomplished by qualified personnel using qualified procedures in accordance with applicable codes, standards, specifications, criteria, and other special requirements.' Criterion X, Inspection, requires inspection by individuals other than those who performed the activity being inspected. Criterion XVII requires records identifying the inspector or data recorder, the type of observation, the results, the acceptability and the action taken on any deficiency. Criterion XVIII requires planned periodic audits by trained personnel without direct responsibility in the area audited.
source: Appendix B to 10 CFR Part 50, 'Quality Assurance Criteria for Nuclear Power Plants and Fuel Reprocessing Plants,' full text from the GPO govinfo CFR annual edition, Title 10 Volume 1, revised as of 1 January 2024 — Introduction and Criteria I through XVIII, quoting Criterion IX, X, XVII and XVIII verbatim. Cross-referenced against 10 CFR Part 21, 'Reporting of Defects and Noncompliance,' same edition, whose definition of 'basic component' at paragraph (4) expressly includes 'safety-related design, analysis, inspection, testing, fabrication, replacement of parts, or consulting services... whether these services are performed by the component supplier or others.' Accessed 21 Aug 2026.

facets.q: What must a quality manual ndt section contain under 10 CFR 50 Appendix B?
facets.a: It has to satisfy 10 CFR 50 Appendix B as U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission enforces it: where the NDT programme sits inside the firm’s quality system, and how it is controlled. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the quality manual ndt section for 10 CFR 50 Appendix B?
facets.a: The management representative. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a 10 CFR 50 Appendix B auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must 10 CFR 50 Appendix B records be kept?
facets.a: Appendix B sets no expiry — it is a standing regulatory requirement, not a certificate. What recurs is verification. Criterion XVIII requires a comprehensive system of planned and periodic audits, and Criterion VII requires the licensee to assess the effectiveness of a supplier's quality control 'at intervals consistent with the importance, complexity, and quantity of the product or services.' For NDT service suppliers this normally lands on the joint utility audit cycle — NUPIC runs most vendors on a 33-month schedule — supplemented by annual internal audits. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy 10 CFR 50 Appendix B?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a 10 CFR 50 Appendix B audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: QA manual written to the eighteen criteria in the abstract with no procedure translating Criterion IX into control of NDE special processes at the working level

sections.heading: Where this sits in the 10 CFR 50 Appendix B evidence pack
items: Quality assurance program description covering all eighteen criteria, with the organisational chart and delegated authorities required by Criterion I
Documented instructions, procedures and drawings for activities affecting quality, with quantitative or qualitative acceptance criteria (Criterion V)
Special process procedures for nondestructive testing, with evidence the procedures and the personnel are qualified (Criterion IX)
Inspection program showing inspection is performed by individuals other than those who performed the work, and identifying any mandatory hold points (Criterion X)
Procurement documents imposing the applicable regulatory, code and QA requirements on sub-tier suppliers (Criterion IV) and the supplier evaluation and assessment records required by Criterion VII
Calibration and control records for measuring and test equipment (Criterion XII)

Nonconformance and corrective action records, with the cause and the action to preclude repetition documented and reported to management for significant conditions adverse to quality (Criteria XV and XVI)

Inspection and test records identifying the inspector or data recorder, the type of observation, the results, the acceptability and the action taken on deficiencies, plus qualifications of personnel, procedures and equipment (Criterion XVII)
Internal audit plan, checklists, reports and reaudit records demonstrating a comprehensive system of planned and periodic audits (Criterion XVIII)

sections.heading: Personnel certification context
paragraphs: Appendix B is method-agnostic and names no certification scheme: Criterion IX simply requires qualified personnel and qualified procedures 'in accordance with applicable codes, standards, specifications.' The scheme therefore comes from whatever code the licensee imposes — in practice ASME Section XI with ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189, or NQA-1. That makes certification employer-based: the supplier writes and owns the written practice and signs the certificates. An outsourced Level III can author and approve the written practice and the NDE procedures and can administer examinations, but Criterion I requires that whoever performs quality assurance verification have organisational freedom and sufficient independence, and the supplier's own management retains the responsibility.

title: UT Requirements Under 10 CFR 50 Appendix B
description: What 10 CFR 50 Appendix B requires for Ultrasonic Testing: procedure approval, personnel qualification, equipment evidence and what an auditor samples.
h1: Ultrasonic Testing (UT) Requirements Under 10 CFR 50 Appendix B

Criterion X, Inspection, requires inspection by individuals other than those who performed the activity being inspected. Criterion XVII requires records identifying the inspector or data recorder, the type of observation, the results, the acceptability and the action taken on any deficiency. Criterion XVIII requires planned periodic audits by trained personnel without direct responsibility in the area audited.
