facets.q: Does ABS Service Supplier require a separate procedure for RT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a RT procedure under ABS Service Supplier?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in RT. Because ABS Service Supplier accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover RT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What RT records does a ABS Service Supplier audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's RT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — source or tube, exposure devices, film or detectors, densitometers, IQIs and the survey meters used to control the area. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common RT finding at audit?
facets.a: IQI sensitivity not achieved, or radiation area control records missing for the shot. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under ABS Service Supplier is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform RT under ABS Service Supplier?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does RT need under ABS Service Supplier?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do RT requirements differ from the other methods in ABS Service Supplier?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. ABS Service Supplier also covers UT (hull gauging and ultrasonic thickness measurement), UT (weld examination), MT, PT, VT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for DNV AoSS compliance?

facets.q: How often is DNV AoSS renewed?

facets.q: What are the most common DNV AoSS findings?

facets.q: How long does DNV AoSS audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does DNV AS (DNV Maritime), Høvik, Norway; certificates issued by DNV surveyors look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common DNV AoSS findings?
facets.a: A technician performing UTM whose name is not on the certificate appendix, because a certificate revision was never requested, UTM reports not produced through DNV's mandated Pegasus reporting tool for fleet-in-service vessels, Work performed from an office not listed among the subsidiary offices on the certificate, Measurement performed outside the granted category or outside the class programme scope on the certificate. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the DNV AoSS audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a DNV AoSS finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does DNV AoSS require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first DNV AoSS audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

answer: Visual is the method most often performed without a written procedure, and it is exactly as procedure-bound as the others — including the illumination level actually measured at the surface. DNV AoSS, enforced by DNV AS (DNV Maritime), Høvik, Norway; certificates issued by DNV surveyors: Employer-based ASNT certification is accepted in practice for ship thickness measurement: DNV certificates issued under DNV-CP-0620 name authorised.
expansion: An auditor examining VT asks for light meters, measuring aids, mirrors and borescopes where remote viewing is used. DNV's scheme issues an Approval of Service Suppliers certificate on form code AOSS 101, carrying an AOSS-format certificate number, a revision number, the service granted, the class programme it was granted under, and a category. Thickness measurement certificates are issued in accordance with Class Programme DNV-CP-0620 and typically carry Category I, authorising measurement on all types and sizes of ships; the certificate states it will be accepted for use with all rule sets published by DNV. Non-destructive testing on offshore projects and offshore units or components is granted under Class Programmes DNV-CP-0484 and DNV-CP-0640. Certificates list four explicit grounds for withdrawal.
source: Three DNV-issued Approval of Service Suppliers certificates read in full: certificate AOSS0000ANW (Lloyd Werft Bremerhaven, thickness measurements on ships and mobile offshore units, Class Programme DNVGL-CP-0484, valid 2022-04-27 to 2025-04-26, form AOSS 101 rev 2021-03); certificate AOSS0000GND (International Inspection LLC, Seatac USA, thickness measurements, Class Programme DNV-CP-0620, valid 2023-03-25 to 2026-03-24, with appendix listing subsidiary offices and 17 named operators by ASNT level); certificate AOSS0000M2J (Check Your Ship OÜ, thickness measurements, DNV-CP-0620, issued 2025-12-16, form AOSS 101 rev 2024-10). DNV-CP-0484 and DNV-CP-0640 confirmed as the offshore NDT class programmes via DNV's own service pages and a supplier's published DNV approval announcement. DNV's UTM page confirms Pegasus as the mandatory UTM reporting tool for fleet-in-service vessels from 1 July 2017. The full text of DNV-CP-0620, DNV-CP-0484 and DNV-CP-0640 sits behind DNV's rules portal and was not read. Verified August 2026.

facets.q: Does DNV AoSS require a separate procedure for VT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a VT procedure under DNV AoSS?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in VT. Because DNV AoSS accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover VT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What VT records does a DNV AoSS audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's VT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — light meters, measuring aids, mirrors and borescopes where remote viewing is used. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common VT finding at audit?
facets.a: Illumination at the surface never measured, or near-vision acuity test lapsed. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under DNV AoSS is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform VT under DNV AoSS?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does VT need under DNV AoSS?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do VT requirements differ from the other methods in DNV AoSS?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. DNV AoSS also covers UT (ultrasonic thickness measurement of ship structures), UT and advanced UT for offshore components, MT, PT, ET and ACFM, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for VT
paragraphs: Employer-based ASNT certification is accepted in practice for ship thickness measurement: DNV certificates issued under DNV-CP-0620 name authorised personnel individually in an appendix under the heading "Operator ASNT Level", recording each as Level II and flagging those additionally designated Supervisor. Because the individuals appear on the class certificate, adding or losing a technician is a certificate revision, not an internal HR matter — the certificate itself states that any alteration to the certified service operation system, including changes to UTM operators, must be reported to DNV immediately. The offshore NDT class programmes test that the supplier uses appropriate procedures and holds qualified and certified personnel governed by a written practice; an outsourced Level III can own that written practice and the procedures.

title: T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Any activity performing NDT under a NAVSEA contract or on Navy ships and systems — government and commercial shipyards, regional maintenance centres, trident refit.
h1: T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Any activity performing NDT under a NAVSEA contract or on Navy ships and systems — government and commercial shipyards, regional maintenance centres, trident refit facilities, intermediate maintenance activities and their NDT subcontractors. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: "Activity" is defined as all sites of an organisation under the same quality assurance management using the same quality assurance plan, which is what determines how many written practices and Examiner appointments a multi-site inspection company actually needs. The document usually spoken of as "NAVSEA T9074" is not a single publication — T9074 is a series prefix. The NDT requirement is NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, Revision 1, dated 11 September 2014, Requirements for Nondestructive Testing Methods, which supersedes the 30 April 1997 original and its Advanced Change Notice 1 of 16 February 1999. It sets the minimum requirements to qualify NDT personnel, procedures and equipment, and covers radiographic, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, ultrasonic, eddy current and visual testing in separate chapters. Its distinguishing feature for a service provider is that it converts ASNT SNT-TC-1A from a recommended practice into mandatory minimums, then layers Navy-specific controls on top.
source: NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, Revision 1, 11 September 2014, 116 pages, Distribution Statement A (approved for public release, distribution unlimited) — Chapter 1 (Scope; 1.5 definitions; 1.6 nondestructive test personnel certification; 1.7 procedure qualification and approval) and Chapter 2 (Applicable Documents) read in full. Related documents cited within it include MIL-STD-2132, NAVSEA S9074-AR-GIB-010/278 and NAVSEA S9086-CH-STM-020 Chapter 074 Volume 2. Revision 1 is the revision attached to current Navy solicitations; no Revision 2 was found. Verified August 2026.

facets.q: Who does T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 apply to?
facets.a: Any activity performing NDT under a NAVSEA contract or on Navy ships and systems — government and commercial shipyards, regional maintenance centres, trident refit facilities, intermediate maintenance activities and their NDT subcontractors. "Activity" is defined as all sites of an organisation under the same quality assurance management using the same quality assurance plan, which is what determines how many written practices and Examiner appointments a multi-site inspection company actually needs.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 compliance?
facets.a: Yes. T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 audit ask for?
facets.a: The activity's written practice for NDT personnel training, examination and certification, provided to the Government inspector on request, A written NDT procedure for each method performed, carrying a certification statement signed by the cognizant Examiner, Procedure qualification data showing that known natural or artificial discontinuities near the accept/reject threshold can be reliably detected and evaluated, Records of qualification training and experience obtained before initial certification, retained as long as personnel remain certified, Results of all current examinations, correlatable to the examination administered, plus a master copy of each examination. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 renewed?
facets.a: NDT Operators and Inspectors are recertified by examination at intervals not greater than three years; Examiners at intervals not greater than five years. A certification is considered expired on the last day of the month in which recertification is due. Recertification by evidence of continuing satisfactory technical performance, or on the basis of ASNT certifications granted without examination, is not permitted. Operators and Inspectors who have not satisfied the annual oversight requirement must be re-examined by an approved practical examination administered by the activity's Examiner. Vision tests are annual, or sooner after eye surgery or other conditions affecting vision. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 findings?
facets.a: Written practice reproduces SNT-TC-1A verbatim without adopting the modifications the publication imposes, so training hours or examination content fall short of the mandatory minimums, The Examiner's specific examination was prepared or administered by the Examiner himself rather than independently by the employing activity, Recertification granted on continuing satisfactory performance, or on an ASNT certification issued without examination — both expressly prohibited, No documented annual oversight, or no technical performance evaluation before the end of the second year of the certification cycle. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 cover?
facets.a: RT, MT, PT, UT, ET, VT, Computed radiography. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271
paragraphs: Employer-based and deliberately non-portable. Personnel are certified under the activity's own written practice, developed as required by ASNT SNT-TC-1A, which the publication invokes as mandatory minimum requirements and states shall not be considered recommendations or guidelines. The Level III is called the NDT Examiner: the activity delegates to that individual the responsibility and authority to examine and certify its NDT personnel and to approve NDT procedures and workmanship standards, so an outsourced Level III can hold the role. The catch sits in 1.6.2.1 — the Examiner's specific examination must be prepared, approved and administered by the employing activity, independent of the Examiner being tested. Transfer of NDT certifications between activities is prohibited except as authorised by NAVSEA.

Activity writes or updates its written practice to SNT-TC-1A as modified by the publication, and delegates the Level III NDT Examiner role

Examiner is examined — basic and method examinations administered by the employing activity, ASNT or another outside agency, plus a specific examination the activity prepares, approves and administers independently of him
Examiner certifies Operators and Inspectors, writes and signs the NDT procedures, and qualifies each procedure by demonstration on known discontinuities
Government inspector reviews the written practice, procedures and personnel records on request, and may require a demonstration of the procedure at any time
Annual oversight by the Examiner, with a technical performance evaluation performed before the end of the second year of the certification cycle

facets.q: How long does T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA); enforced in the field by the cognizant Government inspector — the Supervisor of Shipbuilding at a commercial shipyard, the Shipyard Commander at a government yard look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 findings?
facets.a: Written practice reproduces SNT-TC-1A verbatim without adopting the modifications the publication imposes, so training hours or examination content fall short of the mandatory minimums, The Examiner's specific examination was prepared or administered by the Examiner himself rather than independently by the employing activity, Recertification granted on continuing satisfactory performance, or on an ASNT certification issued without examination — both expressly prohibited, No documented annual oversight, or no technical performance evaluation before the end of the second year of the certification cycle. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

facets.q: Does T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 require a separate procedure for RT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a RT procedure under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in RT. Because T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover RT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What RT records does a T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's RT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — source or tube, exposure devices, film or detectors, densitometers, IQIs and the survey meters used to control the area. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common RT finding at audit?
facets.a: IQI sensitivity not achieved, or radiation area control records missing for the shot. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform RT under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does RT need under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do RT requirements differ from the other methods in T9074-AS-GIB-010/271?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 also covers MT, PT, UT, ET, VT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

facets.q: Does T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 require a separate procedure for PT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a PT procedure under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in PT. Because T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover PT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What PT records does a T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's PT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — penetrant, developer, cleaner and emulsifier batch records, plus the light meters for the inspection environment. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common PT finding at audit?
facets.a: Batch certificates missing for consumables used, or dwell time not recorded. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform PT under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does PT need under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do PT requirements differ from the other methods in T9074-AS-GIB-010/271?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 also covers RT, MT, UT, ET, VT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for PT
paragraphs: Employer-based and deliberately non-portable. Personnel are certified under the activity's own written practice, developed as required by ASNT SNT-TC-1A, which the publication invokes as mandatory minimum requirements and states shall not be considered recommendations or guidelines. The Level III is called the NDT Examiner: the activity delegates to that individual the responsibility and authority to examine and certify its NDT personnel and to approve NDT procedures and workmanship standards, so an outsourced Level III can hold the role. The catch sits in 1.6.2.1 — the Examiner's specific examination must be prepared, approved and administered by the employing activity, independent of the Examiner being tested. Transfer of NDT certifications between activities is prohibited except as authorised by NAVSEA.

h1: Ultrasonic Testing (UT) Requirements Under T9074-AS-GIB-010/271
answer: Sensitivity setting is the auditable step: the reference block used must itself be in calibration and traceable, and its identity recorded on the report. T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, enforced by Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA); enforced in the field by the cognizant.: Employer-based and deliberately non-portable.
expansion: An auditor examining UT asks for instrument, probes, cables, couplant, and the calibration and reference blocks used to set sensitivity. title: AAR M-1003 Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Facilities supplying materials, products or services for North American railway interchange service whose activity appears in Appendix A of MSRP Section J — includin
h1: AAR M-1003 Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Facilities supplying materials, products or services for North American railway interchange service whose activity appears in Appendix A of MSRP Section J — including wheel and axle shops, tank car maintenance and modification facilities, heavy repair shops and repair tracks. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: Facilities supplying materials, products or services for North American railway interchange service whose activity appears in Appendix A of MSRP Section J — including wheel and axle shops, tank car maintenance and modification facilities, heavy repair shops and repair tracks, and manufacturers of wheels, axles, couplers, yokes and freight cars. Certification attaches to the individual facility and to specific activity codes, not to the corporate entity. M-1003 is a quality assurance certification for the shop, not an NDT credential. It requires the facility to implement a documented quality assurance programme meeting the twenty-four elements of Chapter 2 and to be audited against them on a three-year cycle. NDT enters through Element 2.15, Process Control, which requires special processes to be performed in accordance with applicable codes, standards, specifications and governmental and contractual requirements by qualified personnel using qualified equipment and procedures; and through Element 2.22, Training, which requires special-process personnel to hold both training and applicable work experience.

facets.q: Who does AAR M-1003 apply to?
facets.a: Facilities supplying materials, products or services for North American railway interchange service whose activity appears in Appendix A of MSRP Section J — including wheel and axle shops, tank car maintenance and modification facilities, heavy repair shops and repair tracks, and manufacturers of wheels, axles, couplers, yokes and freight cars. Certification attaches to the individual facility and to specific activity codes, not to the corporate entity.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for AAR M-1003 compliance?
facets.a: Yes. AAR M-1003 accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a AAR M-1003 audit ask for?
facets.a: Quality Assurance Manual, Completed Quality Assurance Program Evaluation (QAPE) checklist, identifying the corresponding line item of the facility's programme against each requirement in M-1003 Chapter 2, Production, inspection and test plan (Element 2.5), identifying every inspection and test point, the characteristics inspected and the acceptance criteria, Special process procedures with the personnel, equipment and procedure qualifications required by paragraph 2.15.1.10, Training records for qualified personnel, retained as long as they remain qualified or as otherwise specified. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is AAR M-1003 renewed?
facets.a: Each M-1003 certification runs three years, subject to annual compliance audits: after initial certification there is a minimum of two annual compliance audits followed by a recertification audit at the end of the third year. Initial and recertification audits cover all twenty-four Chapter 2 elements; compliance audits cover six to eight, always including the four the Quality Assurance Committee mandates for that year (2.5, 2.6, 2.11 and 2.12 for 2026; 2.5, 2.7, 2.8 and 2.21 for 2024). AAR states approximate audit costs for North American facilities of between $6,000 and $12,000 for certification and recertification audits and between $4,000 and $8,000 for compliance audits, with exact fees published in Appendix E of the AAR Office Manual. Time from completed application to initial certification varies from four to nine months. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common AAR M-1003 findings?
facets.a: QAPE checklist does not identify a specific line item of the facility's own programme against each Chapter 2 requirement, Special process personnel qualified on training alone, with no evidence of the applicable work experience Element 2.22 also requires, NDT or welding personnel, procedures and equipment not shown to be qualified as paragraph 2.15.1.10 requires, Measuring and testing equipment found out of calibration with no documented assessment of the validity of previous inspection and test results. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does AAR M-1003 cover?
facets.a: MT, UT, PT, VT, RT. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under AAR M-1003
paragraphs: Employer-based, and unusually open. M-1003 does not name ASNT SNT-TC-1A, ANSI/ASNT CP-189 or ISO 9712. It requires that special processes be performed by qualified personnel using qualified equipment and procedures in accordance with whatever code, standard or specification actually applies to the product — which for tank cars, wheels and axles is set by AAR technical manuals and federal rules, not by M-1003 itself. Where quality requirements exceed established codes, the facility must describe the necessary qualifications of personnel, procedures and equipment in its own programme, and prove them at audit through training records held as long as the person remains qualified. An outsourced Level III can supply that qualification basis, write the procedures and certify the technicians.

Findings closed through the five-step problem solving / root cause and corrective action process

Each M-1003 certification runs three years, subject to annual compliance audits: after initial certification there is a minimum of two annual compliance audits followed by a recertification audit at the end of the third year. Initial and recertification audits cover all twenty-four Chapter 2 elements; compliance audits cover six to eight, always including the four the Quality Assurance Committee mandates for that year (2.5, 2.6, 2.11 and 2.12 for 2026; 2.5, 2.7, 2.8 and 2.21 for 2024). AAR states approximate audit costs for North American facilities of between $6,000 and $12,000 for certification and recertification audits and between $4,000 and $8,000 for compliance audits, with exact fees published in Appendix E of the AAR Office Manual. Time from completed application to initial certification varies from four to nine months.
Diarised from the certificate date, not the last audit

facets.q: How long does AAR M-1003 audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does Association of American Railroads (AAR), through its Quality Assurance Committee; the programme is managed and operated by AAR's wholly owned subsidiary MxV Rail using AAR Accredited Auditors look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common AAR M-1003 findings?
facets.a: QAPE checklist does not identify a specific line item of the facility's own programme against each Chapter 2 requirement, Special process personnel qualified on training alone, with no evidence of the applicable work experience Element 2.22 also requires, NDT or welding personnel, procedures and equipment not shown to be qualified as paragraph 2.15.1.10 requires, Measuring and testing equipment found out of calibration with no documented assessment of the validity of previous inspection and test results. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the AAR M-1003 audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a AAR M-1003 finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does AAR M-1003 require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first AAR M-1003 audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

description: What a personnel certification records must contain under AAR M-1003, who signs it, and how Association of American Railroads (AAR), through its Quality Assurance Co
h1: Personnel Certification Records for AAR M-1003
answer: AAR M-1003 names this requirement as "Special process procedures with the personnel, equipment and procedure qualifications required by paragraph 2.15.1.10". The QA manager owns it, and a contracted Level III can author and sign it.
expansion: The finding auditors record against this document is: Special process personnel qualified on training alone, with no evidence of the applicable work experience Element 2.22 also requires. M-1003 is a quality assurance certification for the shop, not an NDT credential. It requires the facility to implement a documented quality assurance programme meeting the twenty-four elements of Chapter 2 and to be audited against them on a three-year cycle. NDT enters through Element 2.15, Process Control, which requires special processes to be performed in accordance with applicable codes, standards, specifications and governmental and contractual requirements by qualified personnel using qualified equipment and procedures; and through Element 2.22, Training, which requires special-process personnel to hold both training and applicable work experience. Where no code covers a special process, the facility must define the necessary qualifications itself.

facets.q: What must a personnel certification records contain under AAR M-1003?
facets.a: It has to satisfy AAR M-1003 as Association of American Railroads (AAR), through its Quality Assurance Committee; the programme is managed and operated by AAR's wholly owned subsidiary MxV Rail using AAR Accredited Auditors enforces it: the file proving each technician is currently certified for the work they are doing. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the personnel certification records for AAR M-1003?
facets.a: The QA manager. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a AAR M-1003 auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must AAR M-1003 records be kept?
facets.a: Each M-1003 certification runs three years, subject to annual compliance audits: after initial certification there is a minimum of two annual compliance audits followed by a recertification audit at the end of the third year. Initial and recertification audits cover all twenty-four Chapter 2 elements; compliance audits cover six to eight, always including the four the Quality Assurance Committee mandates for that year (2.5, 2.6, 2.11 and 2.12 for 2026; 2.5, 2.7, 2.8 and 2.21 for 2024). AAR states approximate audit costs for North American facilities of between $6,000 and $12,000 for certification and recertification audits and between $4,000 and $8,000 for compliance audits, with exact fees published in Appendix E of the AAR Office Manual. Time from completed application to initial certification varies from four to nine months. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy AAR M-1003?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a AAR M-1003 audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: QAPE checklist does not identify a specific line item of the facility's own programme against each Chapter 2 requirement

sections.heading: Personnel certification context
paragraphs: Employer-based, and unusually open. M-1003 does not name ASNT SNT-TC-1A, ANSI/ASNT CP-189 or ISO 9712. It requires that special processes be performed by qualified personnel using qualified equipment and procedures in accordance with whatever code, standard or specification actually applies to the product — which for tank cars, wheels and axles is set by AAR technical manuals and federal rules, not by M-1003 itself. facets.q: Does AAR M-1003 require a separate procedure for MT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a MT procedure under AAR M-1003?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in MT. Because AAR M-1003 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover MT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What MT records does a AAR M-1003 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's MT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — yoke or bench unit, ammeter, field indicators, lift-test weights and the consumables in use. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common MT finding at audit?
facets.a: Yoke lift test not recorded, or field adequacy not demonstrated for the geometry. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under AAR M-1003 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform MT under AAR M-1003?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does MT need under AAR M-1003?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do MT requirements differ from the other methods in AAR M-1003?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. AAR M-1003 also covers UT, PT, VT, RT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

title: OSHA 1915 Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Employers whose workers perform ship repair, shipbuilding, shipbreaking and related employment on the navigable waters of the United States, including work aboard ve
h1: OSHA 1915 Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Employers whose workers perform ship repair, shipbuilding, shipbreaking and related employment on the navigable waters of the United States, including work aboard vessels, in drydock and in adjacent land-side areas. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: An NDT contractor entering a shipyard is a covered employer in its own right for its own crew, independently of the host yard's programme, and is cited independently for its own employees' exposure. Part 1915 is the safety regime an inspection crew actually works under inside a shipyard, and it is the one most likely to stop a job. Subpart B governs confined and enclosed spaces: before entry the space must be visually inspected and tested by a competent person, in the order oxygen content, then flammability, then toxicity. Subpart A section 1915.7 defines the competent person and the records that person must keep. Hot work in or adjacent to spaces that contain or last contained fuel or flammable liquids needs a Marine Chemist or Coast Guard authorized person certificate. Subpart I covers PPE and respiratory protection, Subpart P fire protection, and Subpart Z the exposure limits tank and hull work generates.

Penalty amounts from osha.gov/penalties. Verified fact worth noting: Part 1915 Subpart Z contains no ionizing radiation section and does not incorporate 29 CFR 1910.1096, so radiographic source control for shipyard RT rests on the firm's NRC or Agreement State radioactive materials licence rather than on Part 1915.

facets.q: Who does OSHA 1915 apply to?
facets.a: Employers whose workers perform ship repair, shipbuilding, shipbreaking and related employment on the navigable waters of the United States, including work aboard vessels, in drydock and in adjacent land-side areas. An NDT contractor entering a shipyard is a covered employer in its own right for its own crew, independently of the host yard's programme, and is cited independently for its own employees' exposure.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for OSHA 1915 compliance?
facets.a: Yes. OSHA 1915 accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a OSHA 1915 audit ask for?
facets.a: Competent person records under 1915.7(d): location, time, date, location of the inspected spaces, the operations performed, test results and any instructions — posted near the space and retained at least three months after the job is completed, Marine Chemist certificate or Coast Guard authorized person certificate where hot work falls under 1915.14(a), Written certification of confined space training under 1915.12(d)(5), giving the employee's name, the name of the certifier and the date(s), Calibration records for oxygen, combustible gas, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide indicators, Written respiratory protection programme, medical evaluations and fit-test records (1915.154). Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is OSHA 1915 renewed?
facets.a: No certificate and no renewal. The obligations are continuous: atmospheric testing before each entry and as often as necessary to ensure conditions are maintained, training and retraining as the employer's programme requires, and retention of competent person records for at least three months after completion of the job. Marine Chemist certificates are job- and condition-specific rather than periodic. OSHA's published maximum civil penalties, stated on osha.gov/penalties as the amounts assessable after 15 January 2026, are $16,550 per serious, other-than-serious or posting violation, $16,550 per day beyond the abatement date for failure to abate, and $165,514 per willful or repeated violation. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common OSHA 1915 findings?
facets.a: Atmospheric testing performed out of order — flammability or toxicity checked before oxygen content, which 1915.12 sequences explicitly, A competent person designated on paper who cannot demonstrate calibration and correct use of the instrument actually in the space, Entry made outside the 19.5 to 22.0 percent oxygen band without meeting the narrow emergency rescue or short-duration exception, which requires continuous monitoring, Hot work performed within, on or immediately adjacent to fuel tanks without a Marine Chemist or Coast Guard authorized person certificate. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does OSHA 1915 cover?
facets.a: UT, MT, PT, VT, RT. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under OSHA 1915
paragraphs: There is no NDT certification scheme here at all, and that is the confusion this regime creates. Part 1915 turns on the employer's own designation of a competent person, who under 1915.7(c) must understand and carry out instructions left by Marine Chemists, Coast Guard authorized persons and Certified Industrial Hygienists; know subparts B, C, D and H; calibrate and use oxygen, combustible gas, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide indicators and interpret the results accurately; perform the required tests and inspections; judge when further testing by a Marine Chemist or Certified Industrial Hygienist is needed; and maintain the section's records. An outsourced Level III has no standing under Part 1915 unless the employer designates them and they meet 1915.7(c) in full.

facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. facets.q: What does Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), US Department of Labor; State Plan agencies in states operating their own programmes look at first?
facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common OSHA 1915 findings?

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the OSHA 1915 audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a OSHA 1915 finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does OSHA 1915 require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first OSHA 1915 audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

title: Written Practice for OSHA 1915
description: What a written practice must contain under OSHA 1915, who signs it, and how Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), US Department of Labor; State Plan
h1: Written Practice for OSHA 1915
answer: OSHA 1915 names this requirement as "Written certification of confined space training under 1915.12(d)(5), giving the employee's name, the name of the certifier and the date(s)". The employer's Level III owns it, and a contracted Level III can author and sign it.
expansion: The finding auditors record against this document is: No written certification of confined space training naming the employee, the certifier and the date. Part 1915 is the safety regime an inspection crew actually works under inside a shipyard, and it is the one most likely to stop a job. Subpart B governs confined and enclosed spaces: before entry the space must be visually inspected and tested by a competent person, in the order oxygen content, then flammability, then toxicity. Subpart A section 1915.7 defines the competent person and the records that person must keep. Hot work in or adjacent to spaces that contain or last contained fuel or flammable liquids needs a Marine Chemist or Coast Guard authorized person certificate. Subpart I covers PPE and respiratory protection, Subpart P fire protection, and Subpart Z the exposure limits tank and hull work generates.

facets.q: What must a written practice contain under OSHA 1915?
facets.a: It has to satisfy OSHA 1915 as Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), US Department of Labor; State Plan agencies in states operating their own programmes enforces it: the document that defines how the employer qualifies and certifies its own NDT personnel. The test is not completeness on paper but traceability — an auditor picks a finished job and works backwards to this document, so anything it claims must be demonstrable on that job.

facets.q: Who signs the written practice for OSHA 1915?
facets.a: The employer's Level III. Because this regime accepts employer-based certification, that role can be filled by a contracted Level III rather than a staff appointment, provided they are qualified in the methods they sign for.

facets.q: How does a OSHA 1915 auditor test this document?
facets.a: By sampling. They take a completed job, find the technicians and equipment used, and trace each back through this document to the evidence behind it. A document that reads well but cannot survive that trace is the most common finding across every regime, not just this one.

facets.q: How long must OSHA 1915 records be kept?
facets.a: No certificate and no renewal. The obligations are continuous: atmospheric testing before each entry and as often as necessary to ensure conditions are maintained, training and retraining as the employer's programme requires, and retention of competent person records for at least three months after completion of the job. Marine Chemist certificates are job- and condition-specific rather than periodic. OSHA's published maximum civil penalties, stated on osha.gov/penalties as the amounts assessable after 15 January 2026, are $16,550 per serious, other-than-serious or posting violation, $16,550 per day beyond the abatement date for failure to abate, and $165,514 per willful or repeated violation. Retention is set by the regime and by the client contract above it, and the longer of the two governs. Firms that set one retention period for everything and document it fare better at audit than firms tracking different periods per record type and losing track.

facets.q: Does a generic template satisfy OSHA 1915?
facets.a: No. A downloaded template describes a generic firm, and the first question an auditor asks is whether the document describes THIS firm — its methods, its equipment, its people, its actual workflow. Templates are a starting structure; the content has to be the firm's own or the trace fails immediately.

facets.q: What happens if this document is missing at a OSHA 1915 audit?
facets.a: It is a finding, and depending on the regime it can suspend the certificate rather than merely generate a corrective action. The related finding auditors record most often is: Atmospheric testing performed out of order — flammability or toxicity checked before oxygen content, which 1915.12 sequences explicitly

sections.heading: Personnel certification context
paragraphs: There is no NDT certification scheme here at all, and that is the confusion this regime creates. Part 1915 turns on the employer's own designation of a competent person, who under 1915.7(c) must understand and carry out instructions left by Marine Chemists, Coast Guard authorized persons and Certified Industrial Hygienists; know subparts B, C, D and H; calibrate and use oxygen, combustible gas, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide indicators and interpret the results accurately; perform the required tests and inspections; judge when further testing by a Marine Chemist or Certified Industrial Hygienist is needed; and maintain the section's records. An outsourced Level III has no standing under Part 1915 unless the employer designates them and they meet 1915.7(c) in full.

facets.q: Does OSHA 1915 require a separate procedure for UT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a UT procedure under OSHA 1915?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in UT. Because OSHA 1915 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover UT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What UT records does a OSHA 1915 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's UT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — instrument, probes, cables, couplant, and the calibration and reference blocks used to set sensitivity. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common UT finding at audit?
facets.a: An in-calibration instrument used with an unidentified or out-of-calibration reference block. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under OSHA 1915 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform UT under OSHA 1915?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does UT need under OSHA 1915?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do UT requirements differ from the other methods in OSHA 1915?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. OSHA 1915 also covers MT, PT, VT, RT, and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

sections.heading: Personnel certification for UT
paragraphs: There is no NDT certification scheme here at all, and that is the confusion this regime creates. Part 1915 turns on the employer's own designation of a competent person, who under 1915.7(c) must understand and carry out instructions left by Marine Chemists, Coast Guard authorized persons and Certified Industrial Hygienists; know subparts B, C, D and H; calibrate and use oxygen, combustible gas, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide indicators and interpret the results accurately; perform the required tests and inspections; judge when further testing by a Marine Chemist or Certified Industrial Hygienist is needed; and maintain the section's records. An outsourced Level III has no standing under Part 1915 unless the employer designates them and they meet 1915.7(c) in full.

title: AWS D1.1 Compliance for Inspection Companies
description: Contractors, fabricators and inspection firms working to AWS D1.
h1: AWS D1.1 Compliance for Inspection Service Providers
answer: Contractors, fabricators and inspection firms working to AWS D1.1 on welded structures made from the commonly used carbon and low-alloy constructional steels — structural steel buildings, plate girders, tubular structures, stud welding, and strengthening and repair of existing structures. Personnel are qualified under employer-based certification, so a contracted Level III can sign the written practice and administer examinations for the firm.
expansion: It binds whoever the contract documents make responsible for inspection, which in practice splits between the Contractor's Inspector and the Owner's Verification Inspector. D1.1 is a code, not a certification scheme — nobody issues a D1.1 certificate to a company. What it does is dictate who may inspect, how NDT must be procedured, and what constitutes acceptance. Clause 8 is the inspection clause and runs in seven parts: general requirements, contractor obligations, acceptance criteria, NDT procedures, radiographic testing, ultrasonic testing of groove welds, and other examination methods including radiation imaging systems and advanced ultrasonic systems. The 2025 edition rewrote how NDT personnel certification is established, added definitions splitting MT and PT indications into linear and rounded, and updated the Table 8.1 visual acceptance criteria for undercut and piping porosity.

facets.q: Who does AWS D1.1 apply to?
facets.a: Contractors, fabricators and inspection firms working to AWS D1.1 on welded structures made from the commonly used carbon and low-alloy constructional steels — structural steel buildings, plate girders, tubular structures, stud welding, and strengthening and repair of existing structures. It binds whoever the contract documents make responsible for inspection, which in practice splits between the Contractor's Inspector and the Owner's Verification Inspector.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for AWS D1.1 compliance?
facets.a: Yes. AWS D1.1 accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a AWS D1.1 audit ask for?
facets.a: Employer's written practice for NDT personnel qualification and certification, per ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189 (8.14.6.2), NDT personnel certification records, or current ANSI/ASNT CP-9712, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or ISO 9712 certificates where the third-party route is used (8.14.6.3), Written NDT procedures for each method used (Clause 8, Part D), UT procedure for tubular T-, Y- and K-connections prepared by an NDT Level III (10.29.1), Inspector qualification records for both the Contractor's Inspector and the Verification Inspector (Clause 8, Part A). Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is AWS D1.1 renewed?
facets.a: The code is reissued on roughly a five-year cycle: D1.1/D1.1M:2025 is the 25th edition, approved by ANSI on 19 March 2025 and revising D1.1/D1.1M:2020; the currently published designation is D1.1/D1.1M:2025-AMD1. Personnel credentials renew on their own clocks. Under AWS QC1, welding inspector certification is valid for three years; renewals are limited to two consecutive three-year periods, and before the end of the ninth year from initial certification the inspector must recertify — by examination, by a Committee-approved endorsement, or by experience and continuing education. A CAWI is not eligible for renewal and may hold that certification for up to three years only. Visual acuity examinations must be performed no more than one year before the examination date or the expiry date for renewals and recertifications. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common AWS D1.1 findings?
facets.a: No written practice on file where NDT personnel are certified under the employer-based route of 8.14.6.2, UT operators certified to a general NDT scheme with no evidence of the supplementary examination on the code's own UT provisions, The Level III who signed the UT procedure for tubular T-, Y- and K-connections is not certified in that method, contrary to 10.29.1, MT and PT indications recorded and dispositioned without applying the linear and rounded definitions introduced in 8.10.1. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does AWS D1.1 cover?
facets.a: VT, MT, PT, RT, UT, Advanced ultrasonic systems including phased array (8.34), Radiation imaging systems (8.33). Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.

sections.heading: Personnel certification under AWS D1.1
paragraphs: Explicitly dual-track since the 2025 edition. Subclause 8.14.6, Personnel NDT Certification, now carries subclauses: 8.14.6.2, Employer-Based Certification, allows NDT personnel to be certified in accordance with the employer's written practice by ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ANSI/ASNT CP-189; 8.14.6.3, Internationally Recognized Third-Party Certification, allows certification by ANSI/ASNT CP-9712, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or ISO 9712. Employer-based certification is therefore squarely accepted, and an outsourced Level III can own the written practice and certify the technicians. Clause 10.29.1 goes further for tubular work: UT of T-, Y- and K-connections shall be performed to a written procedure prepared by an NDT Level III, with Level III certification obtainable through SNT-TC-1A and CP-189.

facets.q: How long does AWS D1.1 audit preparation take?
facets.a: Document work — the written practice, procedures and quality manual — takes weeks. What cannot be compressed is documented experience and records history: on-the-job hours accrue in real time, and calibration and certification history cannot be back-filled. Firms that start when the audit is scheduled rather than announced clear it without findings.

facets.q: What does American Welding Society (AWS), D1 Committee on Structural Welding; an ANSI-approved American National Standard. facets.a: Records, not manuals. A manual states intent; records show practice. The usual opening move is to take a completed job and trace it back to the technician's certification, the instrument's calibration, the approved procedure and the report — and see whether all four reconcile.

facets.q: What are the most common AWS D1.1 findings?
facets.a: No written practice on file where NDT personnel are certified under the employer-based route of 8.14.6.2, UT operators certified to a general NDT scheme with no evidence of the supplementary examination on the code's own UT provisions, The Level III who signed the UT procedure for tubular T-, Y- and K-connections is not certified in that method, contrary to 10.29.1, MT and PT indications recorded and dispositioned without applying the linear and rounded definitions introduced in 8.10.1. Almost all of them are evidence problems rather than capability problems: the work was done correctly and the proof was not kept, or was kept somewhere the firm could not retrieve during the audit.

facets.q: Can a consultant attend the AWS D1.1 audit?
facets.a: Yes, and it changes the outcome. Someone who has sat through the same audit at other firms answers in the auditor's own terms, produces the right record without a search, and stops a clarification turning into a finding. The firm still owns every answer — the consultant does not speak for it.

facets.q: What happens after a AWS D1.1 finding?
facets.a: A corrective action with a deadline, and evidence of closure at the next audit. Repeat findings are treated far more seriously than first ones, because they show the corrective-action system itself is not working.

facets.q: Does AWS D1.1 require a pre-audit or gap assessment?
facets.a: Not as a requirement, but the arithmetic favours it: a gap assessment finds the same evidence problems the auditor would, without the finding attached, and while there is still time to fix them. Firms entering their first AWS D1.1 audit blind typically collect findings that a sampling exercise would have caught.

Personnel credentials renew on their own clocks. Under AWS QC1, welding inspector certification is valid for three years; renewals are limited to two consecutive three-year periods, and before the end of the ninth year from initial certification the inspector must recertify — by examination, by a Committee-approved endorsement, or by experience and continuing education. facets.q: Does AWS D1.1 require a separate procedure for VT?
facets.a: Yes. Every method in scope needs its own written procedure, approved by someone qualified in that method, describing technique, equipment, calibration, scanning or coverage, acceptance criteria and reporting. A single combined "NDT procedure" covering several methods is a finding under every regime that names procedures individually.

facets.q: Who can approve a VT procedure under AWS D1.1?
facets.a: A Level III qualified in VT. Because AWS D1.1 accepts employer-based certification, that Level III may be contracted rather than employed — but their own qualification must cover VT, and an auditor will check that before accepting the signature.

facets.q: What VT records does a AWS D1.1 audit sample?
facets.a: The approved procedure, the technician's VT certification on the date of work, and the equipment evidence — light meters, measuring aids, mirrors and borescopes where remote viewing is used. The auditor works backwards from a finished job, so every item has to reconcile with the report and its stated acceptance criteria.

facets.q: What is the most common VT finding at audit?
facets.a: Illumination at the surface never measured, or near-vision acuity test lapsed. It is a records failure rather than a technique failure — the examination was performed correctly and the evidence supporting it cannot be produced, which under AWS D1.1 is recorded the same way as not having done the work.

facets.q: Can a technician certified elsewhere perform VT under AWS D1.1?
facets.a: Not automatically. Employer-based certification ends when the holder leaves, so the new employer must certify them under its own written practice. Prior training and documented experience transfer as evidence; the certificate itself does not.

facets.q: What equipment evidence does VT need under AWS D1.1?
facets.a: Calibration status traceable to the day of use, covering the instrument and its accessories — probes, cables, blocks and reference standards for ultrasonics; sources and densitometers for radiography. An in-calibration instrument with an out-of-calibration reference block fails the same way as an uncalibrated one.

facets.q: How do VT requirements differ from the other methods in AWS D1.1?
facets.a: Scope, qualification and evidence are method-specific, so the differences are real rather than administrative. AWS D1.1 also covers MT, PT, RT, UT, Advanced ultrasonic systems including phased array (8.34), and each carries its own procedure, its own personnel qualification and its own equipment evidence.

facets.q: Who does ASME Section V apply to?
facets.a: Any NDE contractor examining pressure-retaining items built or repaired to an ASME construction code — Section I power boilers, Section IV heating boilers, Section VIII pressure vessels, Section XII transport tanks, and B31.1 or B31.3 piping — plus NBIC repair work that reaches Section V through the original code of construction. It binds the shop crew, the field crew and the outsourced NDE laboratory equally. Section V never applies on its own; a referencing Code Section invokes it.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign for ASME Section V compliance?
facets.a: Yes. ASME Section V accepts employer-based certification, which places the obligation on the employer and allows a contracted Level III to write and sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. The Level III must be qualified in each method they sign for, and the employer still owns the records.

facets.q: What documents does a ASME Section V audit ask for?
facets.a: NDE written practice for the qualification and certification of NDE personnel, Written NDE procedure for each method and technique, with the record of the demonstration witnessed by the Authorized Inspector (Article 1, T-150), Level III approval signature on each NDE procedure and each revision, NDE personnel certification records containing the items required by Article 1, T-190, Annual near-vision and colour-contrast differentiation eye examination records for examiners. Auditors open records before they open manuals, because a manual describes intent while records show practice. The most common failure is a documented system that does not match what the technicians actually do.

facets.q: How often is ASME Section V renewed?
facets.a: No certificate and no expiry — Section V is a code, not an accreditation. ASME publishes BPVC editions on a two-year cycle; the 2025 edition follows 2023 and 2021. Written practices and procedures must be re-reviewed against the edition the referencing Code Section and the adopting jurisdiction have accepted, since the Code-accepted editions of SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 and ACCP change between BPVC editions. Personnel recertification intervals are set by the employer's own written practice, not by Section V. Firms that diarise renewal from the certificate date rather than from the last audit avoid the lapse that forces a full reapplication.

facets.q: What are the most common ASME Section V findings?
facets.a: NDE procedure written to an older edition than the one the referencing Code Section adopts, No record of the procedure demonstration the Authorized Inspector is entitled to witness under Article 1, T-150, Personnel certification records missing one or more of the contents required by Article 1, T-190, Subcontracted Level III used with no documented acceptance on file naming him as the Certificate Holder's Level III examiner. These recur because they are records problems rather than capability problems — the work is being done correctly and the evidence is not being kept.

facets.q: Which NDT methods does ASME Section V cover?
facets.a: RT, UT, PT, MT, VT, ET, LT, AE. Each method in scope needs its own approved procedure and personnel qualified in that specific method; a Level III qualified in ultrasonics cannot sign for radiography.
